From evidence it is also clear that the defendants are residing at the home of Dr. Rashid and it is also came to fore that the defendants exchanged certain properties of Dr. Rashid and they have been holding and possessing the same. So defendants' claim of possessing the share of Ram Das is not substantiated. From the facts and circumstances and the evidences it is amply clear that the plaintiffs got the suit land by virtue of exchange and while possessing they were dispossessed from the suit land excepting plot Nos. 1601 and 1605 and if any party is dispossessed from the suit land during pendency of the suit and such dispossession is proved, the Court is not powerless to restore possession to them. Order VII, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers the Court to grant any relief for ensuring substantive relief and, as such, they are entitled to get relief as prayed for.</u>
19. Another important aspect of the suit is that the plaintiff initially filed the suit for specific performance of contract for getting a registered deed of exchange for Kha schedule land but subsequently when exchange deed was purportedly registered by the defendants on 27-6-1980, the plaintiff inserted a prayer for declaration of title as alternative prayer and subsequently the plaintiffs also sought recovery of Khas possession of the suit land Except plot No. 1601 and 1605. It appears that due to registration of the exchange deed by the defendants as per their claim, the plaintiffs have been constrained to make prayer for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession. This Court is of the view that the plaintiff can seek alternative relief in the event of changed circumstances and declaration of title and recovery of khas possession can be granted as the plaintiffs have been able to prove their title in the suit land by their documents as they got possession in the suit land in 1952. Even the document is treated imperfect one but due to long standing possession they have acquired title by way of adverse possession. In this context a decision reported in / BLC 255 is pertinent here in:
"Let us consider this case from another angle. If Parimal would have sold his property in East Pakistan and in exchange of the sale price he would have obtained the property of the petitioner Hafizur Rahman in India, then could the sale price, if deposited by Hafiz in a Bank, be treated as enemy property? The answer is no as money had passed absolutely to Hafiz. But then why the suit property after given in lieu of the sale-price as exchange should not be deemed to have passed absolutely to Hafiz? Our conclusion following the said principle is, that in a case like this when in pursuance of an agreement to transfer property, the intended transferee has taken possession, though the requisite legal document had not been executed, the position is the same as if the document had been executed against all who want to threaten or disturb the possession of such possessor. We, therefore, hold that the plaintiff-petitioner has acquired title to the suit property sufficient to defend his possession therein and to get khas possession thereof, if ousted therefrom. Consequently we hold that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error in law resulting in error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in not decreeing the suit as prayed for."
20. In the foregoing discussion, it is clear that the trial court without considering the evidence of the parties dismissed the suit having affirmed by the Appellate Court, such decree cannot be sustained.
21. In the above facts and circumstances, I find merit in the Rule. Accordingly, Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.
22. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.
Send down the Lower Courts' Records.
Communicate the order at once.

End.

lawyer:
Ahmed Nowshed Jamil, with Syeda Showkat Ara, Advocates—For the Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioners. 
Md Lokman Karim, Advocate—For the Defendant- Respondent-Opposite Parties.
parties:
Sheikh Mohammad Mozammel Hossain being dead his heirs; 1(a) Md Mohsin Ali and others ------- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioners.
vs
Saleha Khatun being dead her heirs; 1(a) Khalilur Rahman and I others ------- Defendant-Respondent-Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
At the instance of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner, this Rule was issued calling upon the defendant-respondent opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 5-8-1997 (decree signed on 11-8-1997) passed by the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenaidah in Title Appeal No.165 of 1993 dismissing appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 22-8-1993 (decree signed on 28-8-2993) passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenaidah in. Title Suit No. 37 of 1988 dismissing the suit for declaration should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. The material facts leading to the Rule, in brief, are that the predecessor of the present petitioners, namely Sheikh Mohammad Mozammel Hossain, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 37 of 1988 before the Additional Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Jhenaidah for declaration of his title on the suit land stating inter-aria that the lands as has been scheduled to the plaint was recorded under CS Khatian No. 182/1 and the same was originally belonged to Wazed Molla, Hamid Molla, Mozahar Molla, Motahar Molla, Nabiron Nessa Sr Khuki Bibi in their respective shares. The co-sharers of the said jama used to possess the said land by way of amicable arrangement. Hamid Mollah used to possess 16 annas interest of the said land by way of amicable arrangement. Hamid Mollah died leaving behind wife Tosiron, daughter Khoteron @ Bateron, a son's daughter Julekha and a cousin Wazed Ali.
3. After the demise of Hamid Mollah his wife Tosiron, daughter Khoteron alias Bateron and cousin Anu Miah inherited his share. Khoteron died leaving behind two sons namely Shahar Ali and Rafiuddin. Rafiuddin by way of amicable arrangement used to possess the whole share as they got from their mother Khoteron and thereafter Rafiuddin died leaving behind his wife Anowara and a. son Ejahar as his legal heirs. Sahar Ali ultimately died unmarried and thus the whole share was developed on Ejhar. Ejhar Ali was while owning and possessing his share of the land by way of amicable arrangement, he transferred 0.04½ acres of Land to the plaintiff Sk. Mohammad Mozammel Hossain by a registered deed dated 12-7-1961. The plaintiff subsequent after the said purchase took delivery of possession of the land who then constructed a drain on the part thereof and also planted many fruit bearing trees a part of the said purchased land.
4. However, even then, at the time of SA operation the suit land was erroneously recorded in the name of the defendant Mosammat Saleha Khatun. When on 19-3-1987 the plaintiff took attempt to erect a Kacha dwelling but on the suit land and then, for the first time, the defendant's husband disclosed about the record of right as made in the defendant's name and thus they claimed the title of the suit land denying the plaintiff's title and, as such, the cause of action of the suit arose on that day when the plaintiff got knowledge of such erroneous recording. Hence, the present suit filed which was registered as Title Suit No.37 of 1988.
5. The sole defendant Mosammat Saleha Khatun has contested the suit by filing her written statement who upon denying all material allegations as made in the plaint contended inter-alia that the suit is not maintainable in its form which is barred by limitation and also barred by the principle of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence. Her specific case, in short, was that the CS tenant Hamid Mollah used to possess the suit land by way of amicable arrangement. Hamid Millah died leaving behind a daughter Khateron alias Bateron Nessa, son's daughter Julekha and a cousin Wazed Mollah. Bateron as such got 8 (eight) annas share of her father and Julekha and Wazed got rest of 8 (eight) annas share. Bateron died leaving behind two sons namely Rafiuddin and Shahar Al By way of amicable arrangement Shahar Ali used to possess 0.07 acres of land and Julekha used to possess her share 0.07 acres through her husband Saimuddin.
6. Wazed brought a suit for recovery of possession against Julekha, in 1933 and got decree to that effect. Then Julekha preferred an appeal and after disposal of the said appeal Julekha filed a Review Case being No. 3 of 1933 which was ultimately ended on compromise and in terms of compromise Julekha got the share of Wazed. Shahar Ali transferred his 0.07 acres of land to Julekha by a registered kabala dated 8-8-1943. Thereafter Julekha died leaving behind her husband Saimuddin and mother Hemela Khatun. Hemela had no son and thus she took one Jalil as her adopted son. Hemela gifted her share to the said adopted son by a registered deed dated 28-2-1953. By that way Saimuddin and jalil were while owning and possessing the suit land, they settled the same to this defendant Mosammat Saleha Khatun by a patta dated 11-2-1955. The defendant Mosammat Saleha Khatun by this way while has been owning and possessing the suit land since the date of the settlement made and at the time in SA operation the suit land was thus recorded in her name. The plaintiff has/had no title and possession over the suit land and, as such, she shought for dismissal of the suit.
7. In proving the respective case, the plaintiff petitioner has adduced 5 (five) witnesses, in support of his claim while the defendant adduced 3 (three), who also placed some document- which were exhibited thereto. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenaidah then upon evaluating the said oral and documentary evidences of the parties as placed and produced and thereby vide the judgment and decree dated 22-8-1993 (decree signed on 28-8-1993) dismissed the suit, on contest.
8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said Judgment and decree dated 22-8-1993 the plaintiff as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.165 of 1993 which has been ultimately heard and disposed of by the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenaidah who vide the judgment and decree dated 5-8-1997 (decree signed on 11-8-1997) has also dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court dated 22-8-1993.
9. Hence, the plaintiff-appellant as petitioner moved this Court taking recourse under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (shortly CPC) and obtained the present Rule.
10. I however, during pendency of the Rule since the sole plaintiff-petitioner and the defendant had died and, as such, they have been substituted in this Rule by their legal heirs and representatives.
11. Mr Ahmed Nawshed Jamil learned Advocate appearing with Mrs. Syeda Showkat Ara, learned Advocate for the petitioner who in support of the Rule, at the very outset, submits that since Rafiuddin was admittedly found as the son of Khoteron @ Bateron who had to get eight annas share of her mother on the suit land as he was standing on the same footing of his another brother Shahar Ali who are admittedly the two sons of Khoteron alias Bateron, the predecessor in interest of the present plaintiff-petitioner. Learned Advocate then submits that by that way Khoteron @ Bateron's, sons Rafiuddin and Shahar Ali had the title and interest over the suit land; however, even then the learned trial judge as well as the learned Judge of the appellate Court below were erred in law and fact not recognizing the Rafiuddin's separate share on the suit land which has caused an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
12. Learned Advocate also submits that since Rafiuddin died leaving behind his only son Ejhar who sold his share of the suit land to the plaintiff and in such view of the facts and circumstance, it could not be said that the plaintiff did not acquire any title on the suit land on the basis of kabala executed by the successor in interest Ejhar vide registered deed dated 12-7-1961. However, the learned Judge of the Courts below without considering the same dismissed the suit which has caused an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that since Rafiuddin and Sahar Ali admittedly the full brother who got their mother Khoteron @ Bateron's share of 0.07 acres of land and they by an amicable arrangement developed the same to Shahar Ali who used to possess the same, as per pleadings of the defendant and decided by the trial Court below, in her favour. But the defendant was hopelessly failed to adduce any such evidence in support of the amicable arrangement as she claimed and also failed to prove her exclusive possession on the suit land. In such view of the facts, it could not be safely said that the share of Rafiuddin has been in any way extinguished by amicable settlement and, as such, the learned Judge of the Courts below ought to have decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff, as because, the plaintiff purchased the suit land from the heirs of said Rafiuddin who inherited the said share from his father also. However, the learned Judges of the Court below were failed to consider the said plea of the plaintiff while they decided the suit dismissing the same which has caused an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
13. Learned Advocate however, submits that though the plaintiff by his oral and documentary evidences has been able to prove his title and possession over the suit land, however, the learned Judge of the appellate Court below who being the last Court of facts erroneously held that the plaintiff's has/had no title over the suit land; whereas, apparent from the material evidence on record, it was proved that the plaintiff is holding the possession of the suit land, even though the suit land was wrongly recorded in the defendant's name and, as such, without seeking recovery of possession the defendant does not have to get title over the suit land. However, without deciding the same the learned judges of the Court below failed to understand the plaintiffs' case and therefore their decision has caused an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. In support of his above submissions the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner refers the case reported in 6 MLR (AD) 267; 7 DLR 94, 58 DLR 470, 2021 BLD 163, 1995 BLD 524 = 2 BLC 195 and then referring to 19 DLR 192 submits that the amicable arrangement or settlement should have to be registered; but in the present case the defendant though claimed to have the land by amicable arrangement but no such registered deed in support such amicable settlement/arrangement was placed to prove the defendants case and mere non-payment of rent and wrong recording does not vitiate the plaintiff's title on the suit land. Learned Advocate for the petitioner finally submits that the Courts below ought to have pass a decree in respect of the plaintiff's adverse possession as the plaintiff petitioner possessing the suit land for more Clan 12 years who has been able to prove the same by adducing his respective evidence. Even though, there has been no prayer for such adverse possession but the learned judge of the Court below considering the evidence on record has to pass such decree of adverse possession. Learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner then submits that the plaintiff who later on being died has been substituted by his legal heirs and therefore they may have to get a decree relying upon the evidences adduced and produced in the suit and for securing ends of justice this Court may have to consider the same upon relying the material evidence on record. Since this Hon'ble Court is holding revisional jurisdiction it can examine the misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence on record as well as if there having any error of law in the impugned judgment. Therefore, the learned Advocate urges to make the Rule absolute decreeing the suit upon considering the above narratives.
14. In contrary Mr Lokman Karim, learned Advocate who appearing for the defendant opposite party in support of the judgment and decree of both the Court below submits that both the Court below by their concurrent finding had dismissed the suit having finding that the plaintiff petitioner has/had no title and interest over the suit land; even though, the plaintiff-petitioner claimed that he is in possession in a part of the suit land. On that score, the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite party submits that the plaintiff-appellant, Mozammel Hossain himself has filed an application before the authority of local Municipality to settle the dispute as arose between the parties which has been later on ended upon holding inquiry report for two times and then the said authority directed the plaintiff Sheikh Mozammel Hossain to hand over the possession to the defendant by removing the temporary structures as he build thereon, unauthorisly. Learned Advocate then referring to the exhibited documents as of the review case filed by the predecessor of the defendant, Julekha in 1933 and also the registered deed executed in favour of the Julekha by Shahar Ali on 8-8-1943 as well as the deed registered infavour of the Jalil on 28-2-1953 who later on transferred the same to the defendant Saleha Khatun on 11-2-1955 and to that effect the Sk Khatian prepared and published in the name of the defendant Saleha who produced and proved the same in the trial Court below and thus those were rightly exhibited and considered in making decision thereto. Those have been also later on rightly considered by the appellate Court below and, as such, those concurrent finding of the Courts below cannot be brushed away upon a claim of the plaintiff without having therein any supporting document's of lawful title. Learned Advocate then submits that the deed as claimed registered in favour of the plaintiff Sheikh Mozammel Hossain, in the year 1961 wherein the quantum of land shown 0.04½ acres. But, if so, for argument sake Rafiuddin got 8 (eight) annas share of her mother Khoteron @ Bateron share of 0.07 acres land, in that case, his share would be 0.03½ acres out of 0.07 acres; whereas, the above questionable deed shown that the plaintiff got purchased 0.0472 acres of land from Ejhar Ali but how that could be done, it has not been clear at the trial. As because, the said quantum could not be legally had by his vendor Ejhar Ali. However, the plaintiff petitioner was failed to explain that discrepancy as being held and, as such, no evidence in its support could be placed and proved in his favour. Therefore, the learned Judges of the Court below rightly found that the plaintiff petitioner was failed to prove the suit by adducing supporting reliable evidence and also by placing any valid documents in favour of his right, title and interest. The learned Advocate to that effect submits that in alternative the chain of title was found by the Courts below in favour of the defendant and since the SA record was found properly published in the name of the defendant, the little of her cannot be disturbed and, as such, the learned advocate urges that the impugned judgment and decree as passed by the Courts below deserves no interference. Then the learned Advocate submits that since there has been no misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record, rather, by a concurrent finding upon relying and considering the material evidence on record, in oral and documentary, the impugned Judgment and decree was passed properly which deserves no interference. To that effect the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite party prays for discharging the Rule.
15. In support of his above submissions the learned Advocate for the opposite party refers to the case of Nuruzzaman Sarkar vs Siraj Mia and others, reported in 41 DLR (AD) 106 and the case of ADC (Revenue), Jhalakathi vs Syed Nuruzzaman and others, reported in 6 MLR (AD) 116 and to that extent submits that unless there has been a case of non consideration or misreading of any material evidence on record resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, the concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with.
16. Learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite Party also refers the case of Abdur Rahim Chowkider Gov Abdur Rahman Sheikh, since deceased vs Raji Haider and others, reported in 58 DLR 470 and to that extent submits that in a suit for declaration of title, only production of deed of purchase without proof of title and possession of their previous owners within 12 years of the suit would not entitle the plaintiff to any decree and therefore the learned Advocate prays for discharging the Rule having no merit therein.
17. Heard the learned Advocates of the respective party and I have given my anxious consideration to their submissions as they placed and gone through the materials on record as found with the LCR of the case and the references placed before this Court by the respective parties. It is admitted that the CS recorded owner Hamid Molla by amicable settlement got 0.14 acres of land and in whose demise the said land developed in favour of his daughter Khoteron @ Bateron, his son's daughter Julekha and one Wazed Molla who was the cousin of him. It also admitted that Khoteron @ Bateron died leaving behind two sons namely Rafiuddin and Shahar Ali who got their mother's share as she got 0.07 acres of land from her father Hamid Molla.
18. It is the plaintiffs claim that Rafiuddin by amicable arrangement with his brother Shahar Ali got full share of his mother which was then developed in favour of the Rafiuddin's son Ejhar, who claimed that he sold 0.4½ acres of land in 1961 to the plaintiff, Sheikh Mozammel Hossain.
19. In other words the defendant's claim was that Rafiudddin and Shahar Ali in their turn got 0.07 acres of land from their mother who by amicable arrangement developed the same in favour of the Shahar Ali who sold out the same by a registered deed dated 8-8-1943 in favour of Julekha, the daughter of Hamid Molla's son and upon her demise the part of said property developed in favour of her mother Hemela Khatun who had no son and thus she adopted a son namely Jalil and then she gifted her full share to Jalil by a gift deed dated 28-2-1953. The said Jalil on 11-2-1955 by a Patta transferred the same to the present defendant, Saleha Khatun and upon such chain of title the defendant obtained the suit land by the deed of transfer as above. The SA record was thus rightly published in the name of the defendant Saleha Khatun who thus succeed in the suit upto the appellate Court. Even though she ultimately died but her legal heirs and representatives are therefore substituted and contested in her place in the present Rule.
20. In such prevailing facts and circumstances the learned Judge of the trial Court below upon examining 5 PWs from the plaintiff's side and 3 DWs from the defendant's side found the title correctly vested to the defendant Saleha Khatun whose name as such recorded in the SA settlement. On the other hand the plaintiff could not be able to prove how his predecessor got 0.04½ acres of land by inheritance and then transferred the same to the plaintiff, in 1961. If so, the said claim is to be correct, the record of right should have to be prepared in the plaintiff Mozammel Hossain or his vender's name. But, the record shows there has been no such evidence as to be placed in the trial Court below and, as such, the learned trial Judge dismissing the suit found the plaintiff is a unauthorized possessor in some portion of the suit land.
<u>21. The learned Judge of the appellate Court below being the last Court of fact upon re-examining and re-evaluating the said material evidence on record has affirmed the trial Court's Judgment and decree who upon concurrent finding held that the plaintiff petitioner has/had no right and title over the suit land who is an unauthorized occupant in some part of the suit land and, as such, this Court finds therein no misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence on record in holding such concurrent finding.</u>
22. To that context the decisions referred by the plaintiff's side are found distinguishable however, some are found goes to his disfavour as he claimed amicable arrangement should have to be proved by a registered document. Though, the plaintiff himself claimed that Shahar Ali and Rafiuddin, the two brothers, by an amicable arrangement developed the full share of 0.07 acres of land in favour of Rafiuddin but, no such registered document of amicable arrangement in favour of said Rafiuddin was produced by the plaintiff and, as such, the decisions he referred in favour of such submissions also goes beyond of his assertion. Thus, finds no merit in the Rule and in alternative finds the merit in the submissions as placed on behalf of the defendant opposite party. Hence, this Court inclined to discharge the present Rule.
23. In the forgoing narratives this Court finds no merit in the Rule. Hence, the present Rule fails.
24. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to cost.
Send down the LCR along with a copy of the judgment and decree to the Court concerned, at once.
End.

lawyer:
Mostafizur Rahman Khan, Advocate with Saqeb Mahbub, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
AKM Amin Uddin, DAG with Anna Khanom Koli, AAG and Md Shaifour Rahman Siddique, AAG—For the Respondents. 
Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Senior Advocate—For the Anti-Corruption Commission.
parties:
Tafsir Mohammad Awal -------- Petitioner
vs
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Security Services Division, Minis-try of Home Affairs and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Nazrul Islam Talukder, J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi, at the instance of the petitioner, was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the action of the respondents preventing the petitioner from going outside of Bangladesh should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the impugned Memo No.00.01.0000.502. 01.037.20.21479 dated 04.10.2020 should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents shall not be directed not to create any embargo or put any bar upon the petitioner or otherwise cause any harassment in respect of going outside of Bangladesh or re-entering the country and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. The facts leading to issuance of the Rule in this writ petition are that the petitioner is a dual citizen of Bangladesh and the United States of America currently residing in Bangladesh and an established businessman in the FMCG sector. He is one of the Directors of M.F. Consumers Ltd. He is also one of the Directors of Multimode Group which is one of the most prominent business conglomerates in Bangladesh with a presence in agriculture, banking, insurance, consumer goods, energy, hospitality, food & beverage, manufacturing, real estate, textiles, transportation, chemicals and fertilizers, plastics, IT and telecom.
3. The petitioner is a regular traveler abroad and wanted to go to London to attend birthday of his daughter who resides in the UK. By virtue of a holding a U.S. Passport, the petitioner does not require an entry permit to visit to UK and as such, the petitioner obtained a confirmed business class return Air Ticket.
4. The petitioner went to the airport on 24.01.2021 at 10.00 am to board the BG I flight scheduled to take off at 13.25 am for London. He completed his check –in from the counter of Biman Bangladesh Airlines in Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and proceeded for immigration after being issued a boarding pass. When he presented his passport to the concerned immigration officer, the said officer told the petitioner that they had instruction from their officials not to allow him to leave the country. The Immigration Officer kept the petitioner’s passport for 2 hours. Thereafter, they returned his passport informing that he cannot travel abroad and escorted him out. His Boarding Pass was marked with the inscription “Pax deleted and off loaded by DAC IMMO”.
5. It is stated in the writ petition that by vide memo No.00.01.0000.502.01.037.2016027 dated 19.08.2020 the respondent No.3 ask the petitioner to be present in the respondent No.3’s office to give petitioner’s statements on the allegation of transferring crore of money by opening account in Newyork and London and other various corruption allegations. Subsequently, the petitioner duly complied with the letter under memo No.00. 01. 0000. 502. 01. 037. 2016027 dated 19.08.2020 and made his presence before the respondent No.4. The petitioner came to know that the Respondent No.3 by vide memo No.00.01.0000.502.01.037.20.21479 dated 04.10.2020 without filing any case against him has imposed a travel ban on him. The petitioner was not informed about the travel ban nor was he given any chance to explain as to why such a travel ban should not be issued. The petitioner somehow obtained a photocopy of the travel ban request issued by the Respondent No.3; the petitioner after being aware of the travel ban imposed by the respondent No.3 made representation vide a letter dated 28.02.2021 to withdraw the travel ban from the petitioner. The petitioner on the said letter also stated that he always complied with the request made by the respondent No.3 to attend the ACC office and also provided with the whatever information the respondent No.3 asked him to provide and that the petitioner is willing to be present in future at any inquiry if required by the respondent No.3. The petitioner also forwarded the said letter to the respondent No.2. The petitioner even made representation to the respondent No.1 vide a letter dated 11.03.2021 to withdraw the travel ban imposed against the petitioner; the petitioner again made representation before the respondent No.3 vide a letter dated 21.03.2021 to withdraw the travel ban against the petitioner as the petitioner’s 2 years old daughter is in the UK and the petitioner urgently needs to go to the UK to see his daughter. The petitioner also made representation vide a letter dated 22.03.2021 to the respondent No.2 to withdraw the travel ban. However, the petitioner has not received any response from the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 till date; the petitioner obtained a Police Clearance Certificate from the concerned police station. It is clear from the Police Clearance Certificate that there is no adverse information against the petitioner.
6. Being aggrieved by the travel ban imposed against the petitioner, the petitioner approached this court with an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Peoples’ Republic of Bangladesh and obtained this Rule.
7. At the very outset, Mr. Mostafizur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate along with Mr. Saqeb Mahbub, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that there are no criminal cases filed against the petitioner and there is no warrant of arrest against him from any Court as such the impugned order issued by the Respondent No.3 and the very act of barring the petitioner from going abroad is without lawful authority and of legal effect.
8. He next submit that the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and even the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 does not provide any no express or implied authority to the Respondent Nos. 3 & 4 to prevent any person form going outside of Bangladesh based on suspicion as such the impugned Memo has been passed without lawful authority and bears no legal effect.
9. He then submits that the movement to and from Bangladesh is an inalienable fundamental right for every citizen as guaranteed under Article 36 of the Constitution; therefore, any action restraining a citizen from going outside Bangladesh is a gross violation of Article 36 of the Constitution and is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
10. He candidly submits that even though the impugned Memo was issued long back on 04.10.2020 after which long 6(six) months have passed, no concrete allegation has been formed against the petitioner and no case has been filed, as such the restriction on his travel is completely unreasonable and is violation of Article 36 of the Constitution.
11. He has pointed out that the impugned memo constitutes no assertion as to how public interest will be served if the petitioner is prevented from going abroad, as such the impugned memo does not satisfy the requirement of Article 36 of the Constitution.
12. He additionally submits that Article 36 of the Constitution should be considered in line with Article 13 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which states that any citizen of the country has the right to leave his country and return to it; the action of the Respondents is a violation of the petitioner’s right under the said Article of the UDHR. Therefore, Article 13 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights does not allow any restriction on the freedom of movement on any person even in his own country.
13. He very strongly submits that if any organization of the State wants to stop the petitioner from leaving the country, then it must start a specific criminal case against him and get a custodial order by a court of law under the laws of the land, without which Article 36 will become nugatory; as such without initiating a specific criminal case there is no scope for a person to be barred from going abroad even if he may be required to stand trial at a future date.
14. He categorically submits that the petitioner is the citizen of this country and as such is entitled to leave and re-enter Bangladesh without any valid reason as such imposition of such restrictions is a violation of fundamental rights guaranteed under the constitution.
15. He emphatically submits that the action of the respondents in putting an embargo upon the petitioner from going abroad is nothing but a colourable and arbitrary exercise of power of the respondents and this petitioner fails to understand as to why he as a private citizen has been restricted from leaving the country.
16. He vigorously submits that the aforesaid action of the law enforcement agencies restraining the petitioner from going abroad is illegal and arbitrary and the same amounts to colourable exercise of power.
17. He lastly submits that the impugned memo No. 00.01.0000/502/01/037/20/21479 dated 04.10.2020 has no bearing in law as neither the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 nor the Anti Corruption Commission Rules 2007 provides for any such restriction, as such the impugned memo does not satisfy the requirement of Article 36 of the Constitution.
18. Mr. Mustafizur Rahman Khan, in support of his submissions, has referred to legal decisions taken in the cases of H.M Ershad vs Bangladesh reported in 7 BLC(AD)67, Bangladesh vs Allama Delwar Hossain Sayeedi reported in 16 BLC(AD)51, Mohammad Tajul Islam vs Bangladesh and others reported in 25 BLT(HC)195 and Arif Hossen vs Bangladesh reported in 25 BLC(HC)337.
19. In the case of H.M Ershad vs Bangladesh reported in 7 BLC(AD)67, it has been held that “... the universal norms of freedom respecting rights of leaving the country and returning have been recognized in Article 36 of our Constitution. Therefore, there is full application of Article 13 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to the facts ...”
20. In the case of Bangladesh vs Allama Delwar Hossen Sayeedi reported in 16 BLC(AD)51, is has been decided that “if the Government wants to stop the petitioner from leaving the country then it must start a specific criminal case against him and get a custodial order by a court of law under the laws of the land. If the Government is allowed to restrict a person from going abroad at its discretion simply because he is going to make propaganda against Government policy or because he may be required to stand trial at a future date, then Article 36 will become nugatory. This court being the Guardian of the Constitution cannot condone such practice.”
21. In the case of Mohammad Tajul Islam vs Bangladesh and others reported in 25 BLT(HC)195, it has been laid down that “Therefore such restriction or embargo is illegal and unconstitutional if any other authorities preventing a citizen going abroad without assigning any reason that would violate of fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.”
22. In the case of Arif Hossen vs Bangladesh reported in 25 BLC(HC)337, it has been spelt out that “In this particular case we find that no case has been initiated against the petitioner, even First Information Report (FIR) has not been lodged against the petitioner and the allegation as alleged by the ACC is still under inquiry. We are of the view that before lodging any FIR the ACC has the right to ask the petitioner to appear before them for the purpose of proper inquiry, but it must be done when the person is available. For the purpose of mere inquiry a fundamental right as guaranteed by Article 36 of the Constitution cannot be curtailed by the ACC or any authority. Thus, we are of the view that the petitioner should be allowed to enjoy his fundamental right as guaranteed under Article 36 of our Constitution. The petitioner should be allowed for his necessary treatment and other purpose.”
23. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing of the Anti-Corruption Commission, submits that the petitioner is a dual citizen of Bangladesh and the United States of America; this Court by its order dated 05.05.2021 passed in Writ Petition No.4437 of 2021 directed the respondents to allow the writ petitioner to leave and re-enter in Bangladesh for a period of 3(three) months from date, if no order of restrain or warrant of arrest is pending against him and made the Rule returnable within 4(four) weeks from date; and after the said order of this Division, the petitioner was allowed to leave the country; however, till date the petitioner’s whereabouts is unknown to the court and to the respondent No.2, nor does he furnish any information to that regard before any court of law or the office of the Durnity Daman Commission and as such the Rule should be discharged.
24. Mr. Khan with reference to the legal decision taken in the case of Durnity Daman Commission vs GB Hossain and others reported in 74 DLR(AD) (2022)1, submits that the fundamental right guaranteed under Article 36 of the Constitution is non-absolute right; the right to leave one’s country has therefore never been considered an absolute right; the right may be restricted in certain circumstances; restriction may be imposed on travel in order to prevent exit from the country by persons who leave quickly to avoid due process of law and as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
25. We have gone through the writ petition and perused the materials annexed with the writ petition. We have also heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties at length and considered their submissions to the best of our wit and wisdom.
<u>26. It is now well settled that freedom of movement as envisaged in our Constitution is not absolute meaning thereby that the same is subject to certain limitation. Despite the long standing ideal of free movement, it has in practice always been subject to State restrictions. The right to leave one’s country has never been considered as absolute right. The requirement of restriction to be reasonable means that the High Court Division has the power to Judge the reasonableness of restrictions in question. The reasonableness demands proper balancing of the fundamental rights of the people. It is the judiciary which has to finally judge the reasonableness of restriction. The restriction can be imposed by law only, not by an executive order. The aforesaid view finds support in the case of Chintanmon Rao V. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 1951 SC 118.</u>
27. In the case reported in 74DLR(AD)1, it has been decided by the Appellate Division that under Article 36 of the Constitution freedom of movement is one of the fundamental rights guaranteed to every citizen of the country which cannot be abridged or denied arbitrarily on mere liking or disliking without any specific law authorizing lawful justification for this purpose. The reasonableness is to be determined by an objective standard and not by subjective one.
28. It is axiomatic that there is no provision in the ACC Act, 2004 and the Rule in the ACC Rules, 2007, by which the ACC is authorized or empowered to pass any order putting any embargo upon the petitioner to leave and re-enter in Bangladesh.
29. In this regard, the decision of the Appellate Division is that restriction may be imposed on travel in order to prevent exit from the country by persons who leave quickly to avoid due process of law. However, this would be subject to confirmation by the appropriate court within a period of 3 working days from the date of issuing the order putting any embargo upon the petitioner to leave and re-enter in Bangladesh.
30. In view of the above, the impugned order putting embargo upon the petitioner to leave Bangladesh has no legal efficacy and effectiveness unless the impugned order is approved or appropriate order is passed by the concerned court of jurisdiction putting any embargo upon the petitioner to leave and re-enter in Bangladesh.
31. However, the Anti-Corruption Commission shall have liberty to go to the concerned court of jurisdiction for proper order of embargo upon the petitioner if the ACC thinks fit and proper having sufficient reasons to do the same and it may proceed with the inquiry in accordance with law if required.
32. Having considered all the facts and circumstances of the case, the submissions and the propositions of law settled by Appellate Division, the Rule may be disposed of in the light of judgment and order passed in the case reported in 74DLR(AD)1.
<u>33. It appears from the Rule issuing order dated 05.05.2021 that the respondents were directed to allow the petitioner to leave and re-enter in Bangladesh for a period of 3(three) months from date, if no order of restraint or warrant of arrest in pending against him but the petitioner went outside the country without extending the period of the direction and without intimating the court about the whereabouts of the petitioner. Under the circumstances, the petitioner is directed to be more cautious and respectful to the law and Court of the country in future.</u>
34. In consequence thereof, the Rule is disposed of with the aforesaid observations and directions.
Let a copy of this judgment and order be communicated to the concerned respondents at once.
End.

lawyer:
Abdul Momen Chowdhury (Rifat), Advocate—For the Defendant-Petitioners 
Ranjit Kumar Dhar, Advocate—For the Plaintiff-Opposite Parties.
parties:
Noorjahan Begum and others -------- Defendant-Petitioners
VS
Jewlakha Begum and others --------- Plaintiff-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of the defendant-appellant-petitioner, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 24-8-2017 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram in Other Suit No. 164 of 2016 disallowing the defendant's application for amendment of written statement should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. During pendency of the Rule since the defendant-petitioner Noorjahan Begum and the plaintiff opposite party No.1, Mosammat Jewlakha Begum had been died and, as such, they have been subsequently substituted by their legal heirs and representatives.
3. The material facts leading to this Rule, in brief, are that the opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted Other Suit being No. 164 of 2016 in the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Chattogram on 30-5-2016 praying therein for declaration that Heba Deed No.933 dated was being executed and registered upon a false plea and fabricated manner and, as such, sought for having a decree in the suit for its cancellation.
4. In the said suit the present defendant petitioner by entering her appearance contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations as made in the plaint contending inter-alia that on good faith the Heba Deed in question was executed and registered by the plaintiff opposite party No.1 in favour of the defendant petitioner and having therein no interruption by any one.
5. However, after filing of the said written statement the defendant petitioner on 6-4-2017 filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 read with section151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Shortly CPC) for allowing amendment of her written statement claiming that inadvertently some facts and pleadings were left, due to lack of proper information while the written statement was filed hurriedly. But after hearing the parties the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram vide order dated 24-8-2017 rejected the defendant's said application for amendment holding that the proposed amendment may have to change the nature and character of the suit.
6. The defendant being aggrieved by the said rejection order dated 24-8-2017 moved this Court by filing revisional application under section 115(1) of the CPC and obtained the present Rule.
7. Mr Abdul Momen Chowdhury (Rifat), learned Advocate who appearing for the defendant-petitioner, at the very outset, submits that the Order VI, rule 17 of the CPC provides that amendment of the pleadings (may it to be plaint or written statement) can be allowed, at any stage, if so it does not change the nature and character of the suit. Learned Advocate then submits that it is by now settled that the amendment of pleadings may be done at any stage. He to that extent submits that the amendment of the written statement as sought for herein are mere a facts which were left out from the written statement due to lack of information as it was filed earlier hurriedly but nothing else which would certainly not, in any way, change the nature and character of the suit. Learned Advocate in support of such submissions hai referred before this Court the case of Dr. Abdur Rahman and others vs Bangladesh, reported in 30 DLR (SC) 93 and then he referring to the case of Naiyum (Md) and others vs Rahima Khatun and others, reported in 42 DLR 523 submits that the proposed amendment will not be changed the fundamental character of the defence case. The learned Judge of the trial Court below ought to have allowed the said application for amendment as filed by the defendant for securing ends of justice. However, in the present suit, the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram upon a misconception rejected the defendants' said application holding the view that the proposed amendment will have to change the nature and character of the suit which is mere of his assumption but the amendment as sought for does not disclose any of such change and thus the impugned rejection order has caused an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Learned Advocate therefore urges to set-aside the said rejection order by making the Rule absolute.
8. Learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the learned Judge of the trial Court below in rejecting the amendment application though quoted a decision of our apex Court, the case of Abul Kalam Azad and another vs Sunhar Ali and others, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 130. But that judgment was passed in reference to another facts as was behind in the said case. In the said reported case the amendment was sought for at a very belated stage while the deposition and cross-examination of the respective parties' witnesses had been completed and the suit was fixed for argument hearing and, as such, the Hon'ble Appellate Division discouraged the amendment as sought for in a belated stage as it was created a dilatory tactics. Whereas, in the present suit the amendment of pleading was sought for at the very early stage of the suit when no issue was framed in the suit, in hand and therefore the decision referred for rejecting the amendment application cannot at all attract in the present case, in hand. However, the learned Advocate referring to the decision as made in the case of Naiyum (Md) and others vs Rahima Khatun and others, reported in 42 DLR 523 submits that the view taken by their Lordships in the said decision is perfectly attracted in the instant suit in allowing amendment of written statement for making the Rule absolute.
9. However, in opposing the Rule the learned Advocate Mr Ranjit Kumar Dhar who appearing for the plaintiff opposite parties submit that the defendant-petitioner while filed the written statement has described her grievances elaborately but she later on placed a new case which has directly changed the nature and character of the suit. Learned Advocate then supporting the trial Court's rejection order submits that the referring decision in the impugned judgment and order has been passed by our apex Court which has rightly been relied by the trial Court below and thus, he urges to discharge the Rule. He also referring to the case of Afzal Khan (Md) vs Md Azmal Khan and others, reported in 59 DLR 43 and the case of Abul Kashek Al Asad vs Bangladesh, reported in 57 DLR 51 submits that the proposed amendment of the written statement and the averment of the additional written statement gave completely a new story which may create controversy to the parties and thus it has totally changed the nature and character of the suit and also of the pleadings of the defendant and therefore same was rightly rejected by the trail Court below. Thus, he urges to discharge the present Rule.
10. Learned Advocate then pointing out to the amendment application submits that the defendant in her written statement has made out her pleadings supporting the Heba Deed in question; however, later on by the proposed amendment she makes a new plea that the said deed is out and out of a sale deed, even though it was registered as Heba-bil-Ewaz Deed; because of his one brother insisted her to do so. Learned Advocate therefore submits that such assertion of the defendant has naturally caused the change of her earlier pleadings which is therefore not to be allowed for the sake of preventing controversy between the parties.
11. Heard the learned Advocates who by their submissions properly represented their respective parties and thus I have given my anxious consideration to their submissions as they placed and gone through the materials available on record as with the LCR of the case. It is the admitted fact that the plaintiff and defendant are very close relatives who are the mother and daughter resided in the same compound by constructing three storied building thereon. It is the plaintiffs' case that the Heba-Bil-Ewaj deed as claimed to have been executed and registered in the year 2012 by giving false assurance to the plaintiff; however, she did not execute the same with her willingness but it was done falsely with bad intention and thus, she claimed that the alleged Heba Deed was made upon creating falsification. On the other hand the defendant-petitioner has asserted in her written statement that her mother was being pleased with her love and affection who always take care of her mother and, as such, the defendant has paid-up the money to repay the loan amount due as was taken from a bank for establishment of their residential building on the land in question and since her brothers are the men of different character who do not take care of their mother and, as such, the defendant always took care of her mother and thus her mother was being pleased at her love and affection has taken a decision to sale the land in question to the defendant and therefore the sale was done but as per intention and desire of her one brother who by profession a practicing Lawyer had made the said deed as a Heba-bil-Ewaj deed and, as such, the defendant by making amendment of the written statement intents to include the said facts as was behind the execution of the deed in question and therefore she filed the application for amendment of her written statement stating that some facts as had been left out while she hurriedly filed the written statement in the suit, at the first instance.
12. However, a written objection to the said application for amendment of the defendants' pleadings was filed by the plaintiff claiming that the amendment as sought for has to change the nature and character of the suit. The trial Court below then upon hearing the parties rejected the defendant-petitioner's said application for amendment quoting therein specially the case of Abul Kalam Azad and another vs Sunhar Ali and others, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 130 and held that the alleged amendment has attracted the said decision.
13. Whereas, in the said decision the Hon'ble Appellate Division discouraged the amendment application at the belated stage. Upon going through the said decision of our Apex Court, this Court finds that in the above reported case the trial of the suit was ended by fixing the next date for argument hearing and at that belated stage the defendant sought for amendment of the pleadings and thus the Hon'ble Appellate Division by the referring judgment held that there has been an inordinate delay in filing such application for amendment of the written statement. However, the High Court Division allowing the same has caused an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, as because, the amendment at the belated stage has caused a dilatory tactics in disposing the suit.
14. Of course, the said facts does not attract the present case in hand; as because, this suit was in a very preliminary stage which was fixed for taking steps after filing of the written statement and thus it shows in the present suit that the same was very earlier stage. The Order VI, Rule-17 of the CPC provides that the amendment of pleadings of the parties can be allowed at any stage to prevent the controversy between the parties, if so the proposed amendment does not change the nature and character of the suit. In the case of Naiyum (Md) and others vs Rahima Khatun and others, reported in 42 DLR 523 a Division Bench of this Court by their judgment held that the proposed amendment will not at all change the fundamental character of the defence case. Thus, their Lordships held that in rejecting the application for amendment has caused error of law occasioning failure of justice. Such decision of this Court has attracted the present case in hand; as because, apart from the pleadings of the defendant, she by her amendment application narrated a facts as was behind the execution of the deed in question and in what stage she paid-up the money to her brothers, mother and also the bank wherefrom a loan amount was taken for establishment of their residential building on the land in question. And further that the deed in question has been being acted upon after its execution by creating separate khatian mutating the defendant's share, as she found by the said Heba-bil-Ewaj Deed in question and, as such, that facts has to be incorporated in her pleadings and also to be brought before the trial Court below for mitigate the real controversy arose between the parties.
<u>15. Thus, this Court finds that the learned trial Judge has failed to consider the same in not allowing the application as filed for amendment of the written statement about to resolve the controversy arose between the parties. Since the suit was admittedly pending at the very early stage, the amendment as sought for is to be allowed which do not apparently found caused any change the nature and character of the suit. However, the learned trial judge misquoting and misreading the decision of our Apex Court has rejected the said application for amendment which is very much distinguishable on the facts and position of the present suit, in hand. Hence, this Court finds merit in the Rule.</u>
16. In the forgoing narratives the present Rule succeeds.
17. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 24-8-2017 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram in Other Suit No. 164 of 2016 disallowing application for amendment of the written statement is set-aside. To that effect the application for amendment is hereby allowed and accepted.
18. The learned judge of the trial Court below i.e. the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram is directed to proceed with the suit in accordance with law and dispose of the same, expeditiously.
Send down the LCR along with this judgment and order to the Court concerned, at once.
End.

lawyer:
AF Hassan Ariff with Ariful Islam with Md Monowar Hossain, Advocate--- For the Defendant No. 1-Appellant.
AM Amin Uddin, Attorney-General (appearing in personal capacity) with Kazi Ershadul Alam, Advocate--- For the Respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Abdur Raub (Md) --------- Petitioner
Vs
Government of Bangladesh and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam, J: This Rule under adjudication, at the instance of the petitioner, issued on 14-12-2021, was in the following terms:
“Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Annexure-’B’ should not be declared to be ultra vires to the Constitution being violative of Articles 26, 27, 29, 31 and 40 of the Constitution and as to why the impugned Memo No. 28.00.0000.022.99.002.17.97, dated 19-9-2021 (Annexure- ‘B-1’) should not declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents should not be directed to reinstate and to allow the petitioner to continue his employment with full benefits and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.”
2. At the very outset Mr Md Asad-uz-zaman appearing with Mr Syed Md Tazrul Hossain, the learned Advocate(s) candidly submits that he is not going to press the first part of the Rule which is in the nature of certiorari seeking a declaration to declare Annexure-'B’ the arbitrary provisions of section 45 of 076 সরকার কর্মচারী আইন, ২০১৮ (761610 ৪61 relevant to as Ain, 2018) to be ultra vires being, inconsistent with Article 26, 27, 29, 31 and 40 of the Constitution. Section 45 of the 74414 brat আইন, 2osw (hereinafter referred to as Ain, 2018) authorizes the government to send any government service holder on retirement after completion of 25 years of service as it has been done to the petitioner without assigning any reason affecting the right to be heard and the right to be treated in accordance with law. However, as it is already mentioned that this part of the Rule at present is not required for adjudication. Now the subject matter in issue is the memo No. 28.00.0000.022.99.002.17.97 dated 19-9-2021 Annexure ‘B’-1 issued under the signature of respondent No.7, Deputy Secretary, Energy and Mineral Resources Division, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources by which the petitioner was sent on retirement from the service upon purported exercise of power under section 45 of the Ain, 2018 affecting his fundamental rights as aforesaid.
3. By Annexure-’B-1’ dated 19-9-2021 the petitioner was sent on compulsory retirement from the service. The order is quoted in verbatim:
“যেহেতু, বিস্ফোরক পরিদপ্তরের বিস্ফোরক পরিদর্শক, সিলেট জনাব মোঃ আব্দুর রব এর চাকরিকাল ২৫ (পচিশ) বছর পূর্ণ হয়েছে এবং যেহেতু, সরকার জনস্বার্থে তাকে চাকরি থেকে অবসর প্রদান করা প্রয়োজন বলে বিবেচনা করেন; সেহেতু সরকারি চাকরি আইন, ২০১৮ (২০১৮ সালের ৫৭ নং আইন) এর ৪৫ ধারায় প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে সরকার তাকে ১৯-৯-২০২১ তারিখে সরকারি চাকরি হতে অবসর প্রদান করলেন ।”
4. It is also stated that the petitioner is a skilled, honest and strict officer of his directorate. He has attended many workshops and courses abroad in countries like France, Italy, Malaysia, Thailand, etc. and gained invaluable experience and_ skills. And throughout his service life he maintained absolute integrity which was never questioned and he has an unblemished service record. Due to his strict behavior and non-compromising attitude regarding various issues related to the areas of responsibility in his job, the petitioner became the target of a vested quarter for a long time. And on the basis of anonymous complain, Anti-Corruption Commission (in short ACC) investigated the case against the petitioner and a few other officers of the Department of Explosives and vide letter 17-6-2021 ACC informed that they have completed their investigation and the allegation against the petitioner was unfounded (Annexure-’C’).
5. All ona sudden on 22-8-2021 the ‘Daily Jugantor’ published a very derogatory story against the petitioner titled “ঘুষের বস্তা খুলে হিসাব মেলাতে ব্যস্ত রব”. The story was absolutely false and fabricated and a concoction of real facts. The petitioner against the said news report sent rejoinder which was published on 26-8-2021 in the same newspaper. Petitioner’s wife also published a rejoinder against the report in the Daily Bangladesh Pratidin on 25-8-2021. To put the record straight and to restore his severely damaged reputation for the said news report, the petitioner also published a note of protest in the Daily Ittefaq on 26-8-2021 clarifying the negative factual aspect that has been brought against him.
6. Subsequently to that publication on 22- 8-2021 a show cause notice dated 24-8-2021 was issued against the petitioner whereby with reference to the news report the petitioner was asked to show cause why actions should not be taken against him (Annexure-‘C’).
7. He duly submitted his written reply dated 1-9-2021 describing the real story behind the published photograph and requested the authority to exonerate him of any liability whatsoever regarding the news report since the same was false, fabricated and baseless. Without making any inquiry or investigation or any hearing of the petitioner the impugned memo Annexure-’B-1’ was issued absolutely in an arbitrary, malafide and illegal manner affecting the fundamental rights of the petitioner in general and his right to be heard and his right to be treated in accordance with law.
8. The allegation against the petitioner including the news report were already looked into by the ACC and the properties which the petitioner were alleged to have earned illegally were disclosed and included in his Tax file. And the ACC after a lengthy investigation of the petitioner’s whereabouts of the personal assets and properties have found no illegal gain on his part and consequently submitted the report exonerating the petitioner from the allegation.
9. Under the backdrop of the above facts the petitioner moved this Division and obtained the present Rule.
10. Mr Md Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Syed Md Tazrul Hossain, the learned Advocate upon placing the petition, supplementary affidavit dated 31- 1-2022 and.other materials on record mainly submits that the impugned order Annexure-’B- 1’ is liable to be declared to have been issued illegally and without any lawful authority in a malafide manner in as much as it is apparent from Annexure-C, E and F of the writ petition that initially the petitioner was brought under an inquiry with 15 of his colleagues and were proved innocent in the inquiry conducted by the ACC. Subsequently, the petitioner was singled out and subjected to a departmental Proceedings but that proceedings was initiated neither in compliance with the provisions of Discipline and Appeal Rules, 2018 nor have been completed under the said provisions of the Rules and such apparent facts demonstrate that the petitioner’s fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 27 and 29 of the Constitution have been directly violated which contemplate that every citizen should be treated equally before law so to say equality  before law and also Article 31 and 135 of the Constitution being right to be treated in accordance with law.
11. Further he submits that the impugned order should be declared illegal having no legal effect in that it is apparent on the face of the record that it has been issued to circumvent the departmental Proceedings initiated by the respondents against the petitioner vide Annexure-'E'.
12. Most importantly, as he submits, the impugned order is unlawful apparent on the face of report since it is absolutely a detestable outcome of malice in law and fact in as much as the respondents have issued the impugned order under the garb of a law to circumvent the conclusion of a proceedings resulting into the removal of the petitioner from his service.
13. The learned Counsel lastly submits that sthe provisions of compulsory retirement before was without the words and phrases 'in the public interest' which was subsequently added. The Constitutionality of insertion of the words 'public interest' have been consistently discussed and construed from different angle by the Hon'ble Appellate Division and this Division in several cases. He has cited the case of Dr. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh 33 DLR (AD) 201, Mofizur Rahman Khan vs Government of Bangladesh 34 DLR (AD) 321, Bangladesh vs Mujibul Hague 20 BLC (AD) 177 and Bangladesh Biman vs Joinul Abedin 5 BLC (AD) 169 and so on.
14. The writ petition has been contested by the, respondent No. 8, the Chief Inspector of Explosives, Department of Explosives, Dhaka by filing affidavit-in-opposition. 15. First of all the respondents has raised the point of maintainability of the writ petition on the basis of the ratio decidendi of renowned case of Government of Bangladesh vs Santosh Kumar Shaha reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94.
16. Mr Abu Bakar Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents clearly submits that no writ petition is maintainable challenging any action of the authority which is related with the terms and conditions of the service, of course of the government employee. Since, sending the petitioner to the retirement after completion of 25 years service as per provision of section 45 of the Ain, 2018 is clearly related with the terms and conditions of the service hence the writ petition is not maintainable and is liable to be rejected and the Rule should be discharged outright. He has emphasized that the authority rightly issued show cause notice on the basis of the allegations that was circulated in the news papers which was absolutely in accordance with law. The said provision, as he submits, clearly empowers the government to send a public servant on retirement for the reason of public interest. Therefore, question of violation of natural justice is not at all material here.
17. Further the impugned memo clearly stipulates that the petitioner will receive all service benefits after retirement and for that reason there is no point to say that this act is unconstitutional violating fundamental rights of the petitioner and simply on that score this writ petition should be discharged outright.
18. The petitioner challenges the constitutionality of the action only to ventilate his grievances having no legal footing whatsoever since his retirement is very much related with the terms and conditions of the service, the writ petition is not maintainable as aforesaid.
19. However, we have heard the learned counsels of both sides, perused the petition, supplementary-affidavit, affidavit-in-opposition and other materials on record meticulously with precision.
20. The core question to be addressed in this writ petition is whether under the facts and the governing laws on the same the compulsory retirement of the petitioner under section 45 of the Act, 2018 is sustainable and also whether the same can be addressed in the periphery of the Article 102 of the Constitution.
21. It is the case of Santosh Kumar which comes first for consideration. Of course the said decision has certainly created impediment in filing writ petition when the question invariably related with the terms and conditions of the service of a government servant. But there is also explicit exception that has been spelt out in the said decision itself. In paragraph 149 of the reference it has been observed: "In respect of violation of fundamental rights, there must be sufficient pleadings in support of the claim that the applicant's cherished rights enshrined in the Constitution have been denied by the administrative action for which he seeks protection of his rights and that he will not get the remedy in the Tribunal. It will not suffice if he simply makes a superficial statement of discrimination and /or violation of fundamental rights. A writ petition is decided on the basis of affidavit evidence and in disposing of such petition, the Law of Evidence Act is not applicable. When he will come with a specific case with sufficient pleadings, there will be scope for contravention of those facts by the authority and then the High Court Division can decide whether those rights claimed by the aggrieved persons have been violated. The applicant cannot raise any disputed fact. If on admitted facts the High Court Division can arrive at the conclusion that the fundamental rights of the litigant have been utterly violated, then certainly it cannot sit as a silent spectator to shirk its responsibility but it is only in rarest of the rare cases the High Court Division shall exercise its power."
22. Notably in the reference it is clearly mentioned that question of fundamental rights alleged by any claimant if be mixed up with disputed facts and law then certainly the jurisdiction of the High Court Division to entertain the such petition will be ousted. But if the above mentioned principle of exception that has been thoughtfully made out by the apex court is present in a particular case a writ of certiorari would lie.
23. Therefore, the yardstick and the test to judge whether a case in hand is amenable to Article 102 is the burning question before us in this petition. Our considered view is that in the instant case upon admitted facts this Division indeed can arrive at a decision that the fundamental rights of the writ petitioner have been utterly infringed and violated. Sufficient pleadings to that effect have been craftily couched in the petition. It would be revealed from the subsequent observations and the discussions of ours.
24. In this context it would be worthwhile to begin with an observation from the widely known decision of Dr. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh as cited above. The Hon'ble Appellate Division maintained:
"A government servant's right to continue in service is subject to the pleasure of the President. In English Common Law, a government servant, unless otherwise provided by law, holds office during the pleasure of the Crown. This principle has been recognised in the Constitution of the Republic of Bangladesh. Article 134 provides that except as otherwise provided by the Constitution every person in the service of the Republic shall hold office during the pleasure of the President. The very opening words, namely, "except as otherwise provided by the Constitution" indicate that the "pleasure of the President', doctrine is not absolute. This is subject to other Constitutional provisions. Under Article 133 of the Constitution the Parliament has been given the power to regulate by law the appointment and conditions of service of persons in the service of the Republic. It also empowers the President to make rules regulating the appointment and conditions of service of such persons until provision in that behalf is made by or under any law. Then Article 135 provides two important exceptions. Firstly, a government servant cannot be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank, unless he has been given a reasonable opportunity to show cause against the action intended to be taken against him. Secondly, no government servant can be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank by an authority subordinate to the appointing authority. Although a person in the service of the Republic holds office during the pleasure Of the President, but his service is protected under Article 135 of the Constitution, and it is also regulated by laws or rules consistent with constitutional guarantees. So, the Laws and Rules regulating appointment and conditions of service of persons in the service of the Republic cannot be in total disregard of Article 135 of the Constitution which operates as an exception to Articles 133 and 134."
25. Before section 45 of the Ain, 2018 original section 9(2) of the Public Servant (Retirement) Act, 1974 (hereinafter referred to as Act, 1974) did not contain the word 'public interest'. Without having the said word 'public interest', the provision of section 9(2) was declared ultra vires by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in the celebrated case of Dr. Nurul Islam 33 DLR (AD) 201. Subsequently the word 'public interest' was incorporated in section 9(2) of the Act, 1974 by Ordinance No. VI of 1981 and Ordinance No. I of 1983. The first Ordinance being Ordinance No. VI of 1981 was never placed before the parliament and, as such, it attained its natural death. The second Ordinance that is Ordinance No. I of 1983 was also never placed before the parliament which resulted in the similar consequence. However, the second Ordinance was covered and protected by the Constitution (Seventh amendment) Act, 1986 (7th Amendment) and the Hon'ble Appellate Division has declared that the 7th amendment and all laws protected by the 7th amendment were void ab-initio. The parliament subsequently had passed Act No. VII of 2013 protecting all the ordinances protected by 7th amendment of the Constitution. The schedule of Act, 2013 does not bear the Ordinance No. I of 198 3 and, as such, this Ordinance is deemed to be void rib-initio.
26. However, as it has been already mentioned that section 45 of the Ain, 2018 came into force by making provision of retirement after completion of 25 years of service without assigning any reason in public interest. The chronological development of the law under scrutiny that is section 45 of the Ain, 2018 has taken a shape which is now in operation. On the conspectus the learned Counsel tried to focus that from the factual point of view if the compulsory retirement of the petitioner under the present law have been considered it would be revealed that his compulsory retirement was bereft of any notion of public interest that is to say that it was never done in public interest rather it was merely an outcome of the detestable and obnoxious misdeed of a vested quarter as it has already been expressed at the very outset. Basic principle of natural justice have been totally undermined and disregarded. Therefore, the learned Advocate for the petitioner concludes that in all fairness this decision of compulsory retirement of the petitioner should be struck down in exercise of our jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution.
27. At the very outset it is of much importance to note the sequential facts those finally lead to the impugned order of compulsory retirement of the petitioner. First of all it is evident that the Pandora's Box was opened pursuant to a news circulated in the daily Jugantor on 22-8-2021 highlighting the derogatory story against the petitioner. Right before that in the month of June preciously 17th June 2021, the petitioner was exonerated by the. ACC from the charge which has direct nexus with the news circulated in the newspaper in the subsequent point of time. That is to say after the exoneration of the petitioner from the charges in the month of June, 2021 the news in the daily Jugantor was published in August, 2021 and the petitioner was asked to show cause on that issue on 24th August 2021. Accordingly, on the 1st September 2021 the petitioner gave his reply clarifying his position that he is totally innocent and that the allegations were absolutely false and fabricated.
28. Right' thereafter the order impugned against dated 19-9-2021 was issued and the petitioner was compulsorily retired in public interest. If all these events are taken together we could smack a reasonable apprehension of concoction of the entire action against the petitioner. Sole basis is only the news of Bangladesh Protidin which acted as sheet-anchor against the petitioner and he was compulsorily retired of course in public interest.
29. In the celebrated decision of Mofizur Rahman Khan vs Bangladesh and others 34 DLR (AD) 321 as referred to above it has been observed:
"Now the matter for consideration is whether, in view of the impugned retirements under unamended section 9(2) having been validated in terms of the new law, there is anything left for this court to consider in response to the contention that the retirements were not in fact made "in the public interest" in accordance with the amended law. The learned Attorney-General has pointed out that "no such order of retirement shall be deemed to be illegal or be called in question in any Court." and has contended that though at the relevant time the phrase "in the public interest" was not mentioned in the order, but this gap has been supplied by the amended law which provides that all such orders shall be deemed to have been made validly, legally and in the public interest. According to his opinion, the chapter as to validity of these retirement orders is closed. We think, the learned Attorney-General is not wholly correct in taking such a view. For even in a case where retirement is made under the amended law and the order expressly shows that it has been made in the public interest, yet the court shall have power to, see whether the order is in colourable exercise of power or is malafide or whether it has been made by person by whom it was purportedly made, or the person who made it had authority or jurisdiction to make the order. So in the case of an action validated by the new law, the Court certainly got power to see that the order does not suffer from any such infirmities."
30. Further their Lordships observed:
"We do not find anything to disagree on these views, but we think that the question as to 'public interest' in respect of the two retirements in the instant cases is not closed. When these orders were made the law in force at that time did not require that retirements could be ordered only in public interest. Now that theses retirements are deemed to have been made in public interest the Government may show us from their record that there were materials showing that these orders were made in public interest, particularly when there is allegation that the orders were not made in the public interest."
31. In that case (Civil Appeal No. 124 of 1981 Government was the appellant) the government made some general complaint that some of the incumbents' Annual Confidential Report (ACR) contained adverse remarks but did not specify the remarks and the years to which the alleged remarks related. The respondent, Borhanuddin Ahmed, a government servant stoutly denied any adverse remarks having ever been made in his service records of 33 years. The government could not produce any record to show that any such adverse remarks were made or communicated to him. He further alleged that his file was not produced before the Hon'ble President.
