Mr. Amit Das Gupta, Advocate instructed by Mr. Biswash Chandra Biswash, Advocate-on-Record ---------- For the Appellants (In both the appeals) 
Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedini, Advocate-on-Record -------- For the Respondents (In both the appeals)
parties:
Shree Shree Raksha Kali, the Deity being represent by the Sebayet and Secretary of the managing committee ------ Appellant (In both the appeals)
-Vs-
Mizanur Rahman and others ------- Respondents (In both the appeals)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 8th day of August, 2012 passed by the single Bench of High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5529 of 2000 and 5532 of 2000 heard and disposed of analogously)
full_judgment:
M. Enayetur Rahim J.: These appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 08.08.2012 passed in civil revision no.5529 of 2000 and civil revision no.5532 of 2000, heard and disposed of analogously by the High Court Division, affirming the judgment and decree dated 01.06.2000 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd court, Cumilla in Other Appeal No.43 of 1995 and other Appeal No.42 of 1995 allowing the same upon setting aside those dated 30.01.1995 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Sadar, Cumilla, in Title suit no. 51 of 1991 during the suit.
2. Since both the appeals have arisen out of the same leave granting order those have been heard together and disposed of by this common judgment.
3. The present appellants as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.243 of 1984 in the Court of the then 3rd Munsif, Cumilla, which was renumbered as Title suit No. 61 of 1991, initially for declaration for right, title and interest in the suit property but subsequently by amendment of plaint prayed for declaration of right, title and interest in the 1st and 2nd schedules to the plaint and also for a declaration that the disputed 4 registered sale deeds dated 26.08.1975 and 26.10.1978 mentioned in the 3rd schedule to the plaint are illegal, void, collusive, inoperative and also for recovery of possession of the land described in 2nd schedule to the plaint by evicting defendant Nos.6 and 7 contending, inter-alia that the suit property described in the 1st and 2nd schedule to the plaint originally owned and possessed by the Hindu Landlords in their khas who dedicated the same to the Deity Raksha Kali solely for religious purpose and also to bear the cost of Sheba- Puja and maintenance and thereafter, in suit plot No.229 described in the 1St schedule a pucca Mandir with its surrounding walls was constructed and the Goddes Raksha Kali set up and established there-in with due religious ceremonies, pomp and festivities, for more than a century ago; one Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali and accordingly during C.S. operation the suit land described in the 1st and 2nd Schedule to the plaint correctly recorded-as one debuttar property in the name of the Deity Raksha Kali in C.S. Khatian No.218 bearing Plot No.229/300 and in C.S. Khatian No.600 bearing Plot No.514 as Niskar property; Sebayet of the plaintiff Deity Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee died leaving behin 4 sons Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee, Bhupal Chandra Bhattachrjee (uerenaant No.1), Supal Chandra Bhattacharjee (Defendant No.2) and Sishupal Chandra Bhattacharjee (Defendant No.3), being dead his name was struck off from the plaint; after the death of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee his elder son Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the Deity Raksha Kali; after the death of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee his legal heirs, above stated 4 sons, are successor-in-interest and they have no saleable interest in the suit property described in the 1st and 2nd schedule which is exclusively owned by the Goddes Raksha Kali and during S.A. operation, under the Sate Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the suit property recorded in S.A. Khatian No.277 and S.A. Khatian No.733 in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as a Rioti Right instead of the Deity Raksha Kali; Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee died leaving behind one son Sankar Chandra Bhattacharjee, defendant No.4; in the 1st part of July, 1984 the plaintiff and the members of the Managing Committee came to know that the defendant No.1 filed Miscellaneous Case No.148 of 1984 in the Court of District Judge Cumilla for appointment of guardian in respect of person and properties of defendant No.4 who was then a minor and said minor defendant No.4 is the son of the Sebayet Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee and thereafter, obtaining the certified copy of the C.S. and S.A. Khatian relating to the suit property on 08.07.84 and 09.07.84 and persuing the same, the Managing Committee definitely came to know that the suit property described in the both 1st and 2nd schedule was most illegally and baselessly recorded in the name of the 4 sons of late Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as a 'rioti right' during S.A. operation.
4. Eventually, defendant Nos.6-7 purchased 60 decimals land out of suit Plot No. 514 by 04 (four) kabalas, describe in 2nd schedule to the plaint from the defendant Nos. 1-4. Hence, the plaintiff insti-tuted the suit.
5. The defendant Nos.l-4 and 6-7 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements.
6. The defendant Nos.1-4 in their written statement contended, inter-alia, that the suit property described in the schedules to the plaint is Debuttar property and belonged to the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali and they are the Sebayets through their predecessor-Sebayet of the plaintiff Deity and they used to manage all the necessities of the Deity Raksha Kali; there is no Managing Committee for that purpose and for the legal necessities and interest of the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali they sold 60 decimals of land out of 170 decimals land from Plot No.514 described in the 2nd schedule to the defendant Nos.6 and 7 by 04 (four) registered kabala deeds described in the 3rd Schedule to the plaint and the said sale proceeds were utilized in repairing of the plaintiff-Deity's Mandir building and making time to time repair and in giving Tog' and distribution of Prasad and for other legal purpose with the knowledge of all worshippers and Hindu inhabitants of the locality who are connected with the Deity for their worship; during S.A. operation the suit property was correctly recorded in the name of 04 sons of deceased Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee, as Sebayet who are the successors-in-interest and at the same time they are the Sebayets of the Deity Raksha Kali; there is nothing wrong in the record made during S.A. operation as stated earlier; the 60 decimals of land out of 170 decimals of land from plot No.514 described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint was sold to the defendant Nos.6 and 7 for the legal necessities of the Deity and it was also known to the present plaintiff and that is why the present plaintiff on 4.6.86 filed an application with verification wherein he prayed to delete the 60 decimals of land which was sold of the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 from plot No. 514 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.600 correspondent to S.A. Khatian No.733 i.e., which is now described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint by the registered kabala deeds described in the 3rd Schedule to the plaint: those deeds are very much genuine and lawful and the sale proceeds were utilized in the interest of the deity as stated earlier and the suit is liable to be dismissed.
7. The defendant Nos.6 and 7 in their written statement contended, inter-alia; that they purchased the suit land measuring 60 decimals out of 170 decimals from Plot No.514 described in the 2nd schedule by the 4 registered sale deeds described in the 3rd schedule to the plaint for valuable consideration and the said 60 decimals were sold by the Sebayets of the plaintiff- Deity Raksha Kali for the interest and legal necessities of the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali and those sale proceeds were utilized in the reconstruction and repair of the Mandir building of the Deity and making time to time its repair and in giving Vog, Doup, Pradip, distribution of Prasad and for other legal necessities and the said fact of sale of the. disputed property is known to all worshippers of the Deity; the defendants are in possession in the suit property described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint and they have got title owning to their bonafide purchase for value; because of the sale of the suit property the Deity-Raksha Kali is not in any way looser but it is benefited as her century old Mandir was repaired and Vog, Doup', Pradipand, Prasad was distributed for her religious purpose from the disputed sale proceeds and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
8. At the trial the respective parties adduced both oral and documentary evidence.
9. The learned Additional Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Cumilla after hearing the parties and on consideration of the Evidence on record decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 30.01.1995. Being aggrieved by the same the present respondent Nos.l and 2 (defendant No.6 and 7) preferred Title Appeal No.43 of 1995 and present respondent Nos.3 and 4 (defendant Nos.1 and 2) preferred Title appeal No.42 of 1995 in the Court of the District Judge, Cumilla; eventually both the appeals were transferred to the court of learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Cumilla and those were heard and disposed of analogously vide judgment and decree dated 01.06.2000; both the appeals were allowed and the suit was dismissed. Against which this appellant filed Civil Revision No.5529 of 2000 and 5532 of 2000 before the High Court Division and after hearing both the Rules were dis-charged on contest.
10. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment, the plaintiff preferred two civil petitions for leave to appeal and accordingly leave was granted to consider the following grounds:
i) Because the worshiper and secretary of Managing Committee of Sree Raksha Kali Deity is interested per-son to protect the land of the Deity and institution of the suit is not barred as the plaintiff has locus stall-di to file the suit but the High Court Division committed an error in holding that the plaintiff is not entitled to file the suit.
ii) Because the 4 Kabalas dated 25.08.1975 and 26.10.1978 in favour of defendant Nos.6 and 7 described in schedule No.3 to the plaint are void as the Deity did not transfer the 2nd schedule land recited in that kabala and the alleged transferees failed to prove that for legal necessity the 2nd scheduled land was transferred as such the impugned judgment and order is illegal.
iii) Because it is settled principle that once a property becomes a property of the Deity which is immortal, it continues to be property of the Deity for all time to come and as C.S. record was published in the name of the Deity then it can be said that R.S. record and S.A. record are wrong as those were prepared in the name of the heirs of original Sebayet and as such, the impugned judgment and order is illegal.
iv) Because defendant Nos.1-4 by their own act deprived themselves of the power of representing the Deity, then in that case the plaintiff-petitioner is quite competent to protect the interest of the Deity and as such, the judgment of the court of appeal below which has been reversed by the High Court Division to the effect that the plaintiff has got no locus standi is illegal.
10. Mr. Amit Das Gupta, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant submits that during C.S. operation the suit land described in the 1st and 2nd schedule to the plaint correctly recorded as one debuttar property in the name of the Deity Raksha Kali in C.S. khatian No. 218 bearing plot No.229/300 and C.S. khatian no.600 bearing plot No.514; one Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the plaintiff- Deity, said Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee died leaving behind 4 sons who had no right and no saleable interest in the suit property which is exclusively owned by the Goddess Raksha Kali but During S.A. operation, under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950, the suit property baselessly and illegally recorded in S.A. Khatian No.277 and S.A. Khatian No.733 in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as a Rioti right instead of the Deity Raksha Kali and thus, the impugned kabala deeds described in the schedule 3 to the plaint is illegal and void as because the original Sebayet or his successors had no right to transfer any lands of the Deity to any-body without mentioning the name of the Deity as vendor. The learned advocate also submits that as the son of original Sebayet acted as against the interest of the Deity so the secretary of the managing committee being entrusted to protect and recover the property of the Deity, was not barred to institute the suit.
11. On the other hand, learned senior advocate Md. Nurul Amin, appearing for the respondents submits that there is no managing committee as because the defendants became the Sebayets through their predecessor of the plaintiff Deity for the management of the same; during S.A. operation the suit property was correctly recorded in the name of 4 sons of deceased Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as Sebayet who are the successors-in-interest of the Deity Raksha Kali. He further submits that the 60 decimals of land of 170 decimals of land from plot no. 514 described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint was sold to the defendants 6 and 7 for the legal necessities of the Deity and it was also known to the plaintiff; the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 are in possession in the suit property described in the second schedule to the plaint and they have got title owning to their bonafide purchase for value and the Deity Raksha Kali was benefitted by the disputed sale proceeds.
12. Mr. Amin also submits that the suit land was not specified by the plaintiff in the plaint and thus, there is no scope to pass a decree for Khas possession on a vague and unspecified land.
13. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocates for the respective parties and perused the impugned judgment, judgment of the courts below and other materials available on record.
14. Having regard to the fact that C.S. record in respect of the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the Deity Shree Shree Raksha Kali as one debuttar property in C.S. khatian No.218 bearing plot no. 299/300 and in C.S. Khatian no 600 bearing plot no-514 as Niskar property, there after Sebayet of the plaintiff-Deity Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee died leaving behind 4 sons- Rakhal Chandra, Bhupal Chandra, Supal Chandra and Sishupal Chandra. After the death of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee his elder son Rakhal Chandra Bhattcharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the Deity Raksha Kali. Above 4 sons have no saleable interest in the suit property as because the suit land exclusively owned by the Deity Raksha Kali which is immortal. But in the S.A. khatian no 277 and S.A. khatian no 733 the suit property recorded as a Rioti rights in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee instead of the Deity Raksha Kali. After perusing the evidence, of both oral and documentary, we find no reasonable grounds for recording suit land in the S.A. khatian as a Rioti rights in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee. It is a settled principle that the rights of Sebayet are inheritable but the Sebayet or his successors will never have Rioti rights over any debuttar property. The original Sebayet or his successors had no right to transfer any land of the Deity to anybody without mentioning the name of the Deity as vendor and as such the impugned kabala deeds described in the schedule 3 to the plaint are illegal and void. The trial court rightly observed to the effect “সি এস রেকর্ড সম্পত্তি এস.এ রেকর্ডে কোন ভাবেই বিবাদীগণের নাম মালিক হিসাবে রেকর্ডভুক্ত হইতে পারে না।১নং বিাদীর অত্র সাক্ষ্য হইতেই প্রমান পাওয়া যায় সেরায়েতের অত্র কার্যতা নিস্কলুষ ছিল না। বাদী দেবতার নামে নালিশী সম্পত্তি এস.এ. রেকর্ড না হওয়া ভুল।”
15. The defendant Nos.1 to 4 sold 60 decimals land of Deity Raksha Kali by 4 deeds dated 26.10.78 and 28.08.75 to the defendant Nos.6 and 7 claiming as the real owner of the suit land on the basis of wrongly recorded S.A. khatian though the real owner is the Goddess Deity Raksha Kali according to C.S. khatian. Upon perusal of those 4 deeds, exhibit 2-2(ga) it is evidence that the suit land is not transferred without mentioning the name of the Deity as vendor rather than transferor (defendant Nos.1-4) named in those deeds as the real owner of the property. In order to protect the interest of the Deity Raksha Kali and recover the property of the Deity, the secretary of the managing committee being entrusted is not barred to file this suit.
16. This Division in the case of Narendra Chandra Das and another Vs. Sree Sree Gopal Bigroha, reported in 21 BLT (AD), page 1 referring to the case of Prodip Kumar Chakrabarty Vs. Jamila Khatun Bibi and others, reported in 51 DLR (AD), page-156 held that a Pujari and a worshiper of the Deity who has offered himself to act as next friend of the Deity land by no means be precluded from rep-resenting the Deity.
17. In view of the above proposition, the plaintiff has every right to institute the suit.
<u>18. Though trail court rightly decided the above issues but the lower appellate court as well as the High Court Division committed an error in reversing the finding of the trial court by dismissing the suit.</u>
19. We have already observed that the S.A. khatian was wrongly recorded whereas C.S. khatian is rightly recorded in the name of Deity Raksha Kali. The disputed deeds were executed based on S.A. khatian. Though the right of Sebayet is inheritable but the successors-in-interest that means 4 sons of deceased Sebayets of the Deity Rakhsha Kali can-not sale the property which belonged to Deity without mentioning the name of Deity Raksha kali as a vendor. The defendants also failed to prove legal necessities of the Deity Raksha Kali. Thus, the title on the disputed land cannot be passed by the disputed 4 sale deeds as because the vendors of those sale deeds have no locus standi to transfer the property.
<u>20. Upon perusal of the plaint it transpires that the plaintiff described that the 2nd schedule land as 60 decimals out of 1.70 areas under plot no.514 area which was also claimed by the disputed sale deeds. There cannot be any vagueness in the schedule as because 60 decimals of land were clearly described in the 4 schedule of the said sale deeds, exhibit-2- 2(ga). As such there is no scope to say that suit land is vague and not specified. Moreover, the said issue was not agitated at the stage of trial. The appellate court and High Court Division committed an error in holding that 2nd schedule land is vague.</u>
21. Having discussed and considered as above, we find merit in the instant appeals.
22. Thus, the appeals are allowed.
<u>23. The judgment and decree passed both by the High Court Division is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree pronounced by trial court is affirmed and upheld.</u>
End.

For the Respondent ------- Mr. Shah Monjurul Hoque, Advocate with Mr. Mosharrof Hossain, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocateon-Record

National Board of Revenue (NBR Building), Segunbagicha, Romna, Dhaka, represented by its Chairman and others ----- Petitioners

BSRM Steels Limited, A Public Limited Company, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994, having its registered office at Ali Mansion, 1173/1207, Sadarghat Road, Chattogram, Bangladesh, represented by it’s Managing Director ---------- Respondent.
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 28.08.2019 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.14303 of 2018)
full_judgment:
MD. NURUZZAMAN, J: Delay of 403 (four hundred three) in filing of this civil petition for leave to appeal is hereby condoned.
2. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 28.08.2019 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.14303 of 2018 making the Rule Nisi absolute and the impugned explanation (মুসক আইন ও বিধি) so given by the writ respondent No.5, Second Secretary (মুসক আইন ও বিধি), National Board of Revenue (মুসক আইন ও বিধি শাখা) under Nathi No.08.01. 0000.068.20.001.16/373 dated 29.11.2018 and also refusal of the writ respondents to receive and thereafter return “মুসক-১১” and “মুসক-২০” as per requirement of Rule 27(2) of the VAT Rules, 1991 from and to the writ petitioners in connection with “deemed export” (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) goods by foreign currency through banking channel to the interested purchasers within the purview of section 2(শ) clause (আ) and (ই) of the VAT Act, 1991 in order to transport the products of the writ petitioners under the scheme of “deemed export” (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) from the factory premises to the respective sites of the buyers concerned, are hereby declared to have been done without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect. Accordingly, the writ respondents concern are hereby directed to receive and thereafter return “মুসক-challan” in due compliance of law and to the writ petitioners in connection with the “deemed export” (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) products by foreign currency through banking channel to the interested buyers in order to transport the products of the writ petitioners under the scheme of “deemed export” from the factory premises to the respective sites of the buyers concerned.
3. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that the writ petitioner filed the Writ Petition No.14303 of 2018 before the High Court Division challenging the refusal of the writ respondents, to receive মুসক-১১ and মুসক-২০ (under the requirement of Rule 27(2) of the VAT Rules, 1991) from the writ petitioner in connection with deemed export (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) under section 2(শ)(অ) of the VAT ACT 1991 by foreign currency through banking channel to hundred percent export oriented industries and refusal to return duly verified (পরীক্ষা সম্পন্নকৃত) মুসক-১১ and মুসক-২০ to transport writ petitioner’s products under the scheme of “deemed export” (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) from the factory premise to the site of the buyers and direction upon the writ respondents to receive মুসক-১১ and মুসক-২০ (under the requirement of Rule 27(2) of the VAT Rules 1991) from the writ petitioner in connection with deemed export (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) under section 2(শ)(অ) of the VAT ACT 1991 of its products to buyers those who are paying export proceeds by foreign currency through banking channel and engaged in hundred percent export and also direction upon the writ respondents to return duly verified (পরীক্ষা সম্পন্নকৃত) মুসক-১১ and মুসক-২০ to the writ petitioner to transport “deemed export goods” (রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য) under section 2(শ)(অ) of the VAT ACT 1991 from its factory premise warehouse to intend buyer’s site those who are paying export proceeds by foreign currency through banking channel and engaged in hundred percent export stating that the writ petitioner is one public limited company engaged in manufacturing mild steel products namely M.S. Rod, Bar, angle etc. However, those products of the writ petitioner has been duly certified by Bangladesh Standard Testing Institute (BSTI), Bureau of Indian Standard (BSI), Dubai Standard, UK Standard and European Standard respectively. The writ petitioner being industrial importers regularly import sponge iron, iron scrap and billets for manufacturing mild steel products in their own factories on payment of applicable duties and taxes on the value of raw materials at the import stage. However, they usually sell their products in the domestic market directly and through appointed dealers as well as to some other intending buyers who are 100% export oriented garments industries and also to many international contractors being appointed in mega-projects of Bangladesh under international tender being floated by the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh. In this regard, it has been contended that the purchasers who are 100% export oriented garment industries other companies pay price of the supplied goods in foreign currency following the scheme of “deemed export”. On the other hand, the international contractors who are engaged in mega projects in Bangladesh also purchase M.S. products from the writ petitioner making payment in foreign currency under “deemed export” scheme. China Communication Construction Co. Ltd., an international company was appointed vide international tender as a contractor to execute and implement “Karnafuly Tunnel Project”; Electric Power Construction Co. Ltd., also an international company was appointed under international tender as a contractor to implement “Payra Thermal Power Plant Project”; Afcons Infrastructure Ltd., another international contractor was appointed vide international tender to implement “Maitree STP Project, Rampal, Bagerhat; ”Larsen and Toubro Ltd., an international company was appointed vide international tender as a contractor for construction of railway bridge over Rupsha river; Iron International Ltd., an international company was appointed under international tender as a contractor to implement “Khulna-Mongla Port Rail Line Project” and Bangladesh-Indian Friendship Power Co., a joint venture company was appointed as a contractor also under international tender to implement “Rampal Power Plant” Project. Pursuant to the respective contracts said international contractors were issued work orders for implementation of those projects. Subsequently, those contractors floated different tenders inviting offers from local manufacturers for supply of various materials including mild steel products. The writ petitioner participated in the respective bids with others and having become successful bidders were selected to supply M.S. products as a manufacturer. Thereafter, various agreements were executed by and between the international contractors and the writ petitioner in order to sell mild steel products in foreign currency. According to the terms and conditions of the agreements, the writ petitioner duly supplied M.S. products those international contractors in exchange of foreign currency through banking channel and to that effect the negotiating bank also issued Proceed Realization Certificates (in short, PRC) in favour of the writ petitioner. The writ petitioner also sold M.S. products to some other 100% export oriented garments factories and other similar factories situated in EPZ area in foreign currency within the scheme of section 2(k) clause (Av) and (B) and section 3(2) of the VAT Act, 1991 (in short, Act of 1991). However, before delivery of the products from the factory premises/warehouses to the above mentioned sites of the respective buyers, the writ petitioner issued “মূসক-১১” with 0% VAT under section 3(2) of the Act, 1991 and submitted “মূসক-১১” to the respective VAT Circle seeking issuance of “মূসক-২০” in order to transport M.S. products from the factory premises to the respective sites of the purchasers i.e., the international contractors. In response, thereof, the VAT Circle concern had been issuing “মূসক-২০” for a long time on receipt of “মূসক-১১” under the “deemed export” scheme. Despite the same, subsequently, the Divisional Officer and Revenue Officer of the concerned VAT Circle had refused to receive “মূসক-১১” and to return “মূসক-২০” in order to continue sale of products in the aforementioned manner pursuant to the impugned explanation so given by the writ respondent No.5 under Nathi No.08.01.0000.068.20.001.16/373 dated 29.11.2018. As a result, the writ petitioner has been restrained from selling M.S. products under the “deemed export” scheme. Hence, the application. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case stated above, the writ petitioner, finding no other alternative efficacious remedy, filed the above noted writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi.
4. The writ respondent No.2 contested the said Rule Nisi by filing an affidavit-inopposition.
5. In due course, after hearing the parties and considering the connected papers on record, a Division Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule Nisi absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 28.08.2019.
6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and order dated 28.08.2019 passed in Writ Petition No.14303 of 2018, the National Board of Revenue and others - writ respondents as petitioners herein filed the instant civil Petitions for leave to appeal.
7. Mr. SK. Md. Morshed, the learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the respective agreements were executed between M/s. Power Grid Company of Bangladesh Ltd. (in short, PGCB) and consortium of Fujikura Ltd. ITOCHU Corporation and LS Cable and System Ltd. Subsequently, the writ petitioner concern as supplier entered into an agreement on 21.12.2016 with the said contractors for supplying goods. As such, it is clear that the writ petitioner and the procuring entity i.e., PGCB did not enter into any agreement at any point of time under the international tender process. In this regard referring to Rule 31Ka(1ka) of the VAT Rules, 1991, in view of the said provision respective project must be funded in foreign currency in the form of grant or loan. That project should be under an international agreement or Memorandum of Articles, the consignee liable to implement the project should be a VAT registered entity in Bangladesh; and that the work order for supply of materials/implementation should be given to the successful bidder who participated in any local or international tender. In the instant case, the person/organization liable to implement the project is PGCB (বৈদেশিক মুদ্রার বিনিময়ে প্রকল্প বাস্তবায়নে দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত সংস্থা) who has been granted fund and assigned for implementation of the project in question and that GS Engineering and Construction Corporation, a foreign company being a successful bidder entered into a contract with PGCB bearing Contract No.PGCB /400kv/PAT-GOP/TL for design, manufacture and supply, installation, testing and commissioning the project. Since the activities of the said foreign company had been done in exchange of foreign currency, hence, its activities may be treated as “export/deemed export” provided it fulfills the pre-condition of being a registered entity under the VAT Act in Bangladesh. Apart from that, the writ petitioner although are VAT registered companies of Bangladesh but being the subcontractor of GS Engineering and Construction Corporation have no scope to get the said benefit since it did not sign any contract directly with PGCB but getting its remuneration in foreign currency, which is a part of the sum acquired by GS Engineering from PGCB but the High Court Division committed serious illegality in making the Rule Nisi absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the writ respondent No.4 has issued the impugned Memo explaining the legal aspects as contained in Rule 31Ka of the VAT Rules, 1991 but the writ petitioner by filing the instant writ petition has intended to misinterpret the said provision of law to suit its own sweet will in order to avail duty drawback paid in connection with the input output co-efficient in the guise of “deemed export” which is malafide. He next submits that the writ respondent No.3-National Board of Revenue, has statutory power conferred under section 219B of the Customs Act, 1969 read with section 72 of the VAT Act, 1991 to issue Rules, orders and notices, explanations or circulars in any matter for the purpose of implementation/execution of the Act provided that those are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act or the Rules so framed thereunder. At the same time, Rule 38 of the VAT Rules, 1991 has also provided power to the Board, the Commissioners or the Director Generals to issue explanations; orders clarify the disputes emendated there from. Moreover, the Director General of the concerned department of NBR has power to determine inputoutput co-efficient pursuant to section 13(3) of the VAT Act, 1991 and to grant drawback to the exporter on the duties and taxes paid on inputs used in the manufacturing of exported/deemed exported goods on that basis. Hence, the impugned orders issued by the writ respondent No.5 regretting to approve input output co-efficient prior to granting drawback is lawful. He also submits that the writ petitioner submitted monthly return in statutory form “Mushak-19” stating its activities thereon. However, its monthly returns were duly accepted on being satisfied by the authority since no objection as to taking rebate by the writ petitioner was raised. But fact remains that section 26Ka(6) of the VAT Act, 1991 has put no bar on re-investigation or re-audit of the activities of any tax payer on reasonable ground even though it has been audited or investigated earlier. Hence, the writ petitioner cannot be absolved from any subsequent demand on the plea that the returns were submitted and those had been accepted without any instant objection whatsoever. In that view of the matter, the impugned Nathi dated 29.11.2018 issued by the writ respondent No.4 providing explanation of Rule 31Ka of the VAT Rules, 1991 and thereby subsequent refusal to allow input-output coefficient (মূসক) in favour of the writ petitioner as well as demand of VAT under section 55(1) of the Act of 1991 cannot be mandated as unlawful. He finally submits that Article 65(1) of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh provides that nothing shall prevent the Parliament from delegating its power to make orders, rules or other enactments having legislative effect. Moreover, it is the established principle of law that the Legislature is not always required to legislate in its entirety to carry out all its work. Some of its functions is left out to be performed fully by persons technically conversant with the levy and realization may be frustrated but the High Court Division committed serious illegality in making the Rule Nisi absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
8. Mr. Shah Monjurul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that the words “রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য” as defined in section ২(শ) clause (আ) and (ই) of the VAT Act, 1991 includes writ petitioner’s supply of goods i.e., M.S. products to the international contractors for implementation of mega projects in Bangladesh against foreign currency as well as other 100% export oriented garments industries. In that view of the matter, the concerned VAT Circle as well as Division Office on receipt of “মূসক-১১” with 0% VAT under section 3(2) of the Act, 1991 from the writ petitioner issued “মূসক-২০” with the copy of Form “মূসক-১১” for shipment (transfer) of supplied goods from the factory premises/warehouses of the writ petitioner to the respective sites of the purchasers. The writ petitioner accordingly adjusted taxes and duties following the provisions of section 13 of the Act, 1991. That before 2009, there was no express definition of “রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য” in the VAT Act, 1991, however, section 2(ফ) of the said Act defined “শুন্য করারোপযোগ্য পণ্য বা সেবা” as “রপ্তানিকৃত / রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য কোনো পণ্য বা সেবা” In 2009, for the first time, the words “রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য” (deemed export) had been defined by the Parliament vide Finance Act, 2009 by inserting section 2(ব). Later, vide Finance Act, 2010 section 2(ব) was repealed and was replaced with section 2(শ) clause (অ) and (আ). Lastly, vide Finance Act, 2013 by making amendment of section 2(শ) clause (অ), (আ) and (ই) of the VAT Act, 1991 have been inserted and thereby the Parliament has included the category of supplies/transactions of the writ petitioner within the ambit of “রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য”. He further submits that Rule 31Ka of the VAT Rules, 1991 (in short, the Rules, 1991) was first introduced by the NBR vide SRO No.305/Ain/2004/433-Mushak dated 21.10.2004. Subsequently, said provision was amended in 2010 Vide SRO No.161-Ain/2010/456-Mushak dated 02.06.2010; later, sub-rule (1Ka) was inserted in rule 31Ka vide SRO No.05-Ain/2013/694-Mushak dated 02.01.2014 in order to achieve the object section 2(শ) clause (আ) and (ই) of the Act, 1991 for the interest of local manufacturers and service renderers and also to enrich foreign currency reserve of the county. In this connection, the writ petitioner supplied M.S. products to international contractors who being the successful bidders invited tenders for supply of products in order to materialize the projects concern; the writ petitioner along with others participated in open tender competition and having become successful in the bid supplied the goods to those contractors who on receipt thereof made payment in favour of the writ petitioner in foreign currency through the negotiating banks and to that effect the negotiating banks also issued PRC by informing those transactions to Bangladesh bank. As such, the supply of M.S. products of the writ petitioner squarely comes within the purview of sections 2(n) clause (B) and C, 3(2) and 13 of the Act, 1991 read with Rule 31Ka(1ka) of the Rules, 1991 and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule Nisi absolute and passed the impugned judgment. Hence, the instant leave petition may kindly be dismissed.
9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Additional Attorney General for the petitioners and the learned Advocate for the respondent. Perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and connected other materials on record.
10. From the averments of the writ petition it is seen fairly admitted that PGCB, the procuring entity entered into contract for executing and implementing its different projects e.g. with the China Communication and Construction Limited ‘Karnafuly Tunnel Project’; with Electric Power Construction Co. Ltd for ‘Payra Thermal Power Plant Project’; with Afcons Infrastructure Ltd for ‘Maitree STP Project, Rampal, Bagerhat’; with Larsen and Toubro Ltd for Railway Brodge over Rupsha river; with Iron International Ltd for ‘Khulna- Mongla Port Rail line Project’; with Bangladesh-India Friendship Power Co. for ‘Rampal Power Plant’ through some international tender processes. The writ petitioner Company and PGCB never entered into any contract under the concerned international tender process. Rather the writ petitioner company entered into agreements with the aforementioned companies for supplying mild steel (MS) products which are sub-contracts in nature. To avail the benefits promised under the Rule 31Ka of the VAT Rules, 1991 relevant scheme must be funded in foreign currency in the form of grant or loan; that project should be under an international agreement or Memorandum of Articles; the consignee liable to implement the project should be a VAT registered entity in Bangladesh and that the work order for supply of materials/implementation should be given to the winning bidder who participated in any local or international tender.
11. The concerned rule 31A of the VAT Rules 1991 is as such-
“৩১ক। স্থানীয় বা আন্তর্জাতিক দরপত্রের বিপরীতে বৈদেশিক মুদুায় পণ্য সরবরাহ বা সেবা প্রদান ।-
(১) আর্তজাতিক চুক্তি বা সমঝোতা স্মারকের আওতায় বাংলাদেশের অভ্যন্তরে কোনো স্থাপনা বা অবকাঠামো নির্মাণ, সুষমকরণ, সম্পুসারণ, আধুনিকায়ন বা বাংলাদেশের কোনো জনগোষ্ঠীর মধ্যে কোনো পণ্য সরবরাহ বা সেবা প্রদানের অভিপ্রায়ে উপর্যুক্ত কার্ধাবলির সহযোগিতার লক্ষ্যে অনুদান বা খণ হিসেবে প্রদত্ত বৈদেশিক মুদ্বার বিনিময়ে প্রকল্প বাস্তবায়নে দায়িতৃপ্রাপ্ত সংস্থা বা ব্যক্তি কর্তৃক বাংলাদেশে নিবন্ধিত কোনো উৎপাদক বা ত সেবা প্রদানকারীর নিকট হইতে স্থানীয় বা আর্তজাতিক দরপত্রের মাধ্যমে কোনো পণ্য বা সেবা ক্রয় করা হইলে নিম্নবর্ণিত শর্তে উহা আইনের ধারা ৩ এর উপ-ধারা (২)৫ক) এর অধীন রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে, যথা:
(ক) বাংলাদেশ সরকার বা সরকারের নিকট হইতে ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত ব্যক্তি বা প্রতিষ্ঠানের সহিত অনুদান বা খণ সংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে দাতা সংস্থার আন্তর্জাতিক চুক্তি বা সমঝোতা স্মারক থাকিতে হইবে;
খে) স্থানীয় বা আন্তর্জাতিক দরপত্রে উক্ত চুক্তি বা সমঝোতা স্মারকের রেফারেন্স উল্লেখপূর্বক স্থানীয়ভাবে সংগৃহীত পণ্য বা সেবা ব্যবহারের বিষয়টি উল্লেখ করিতে হইবে; এবং

The aforementioned foreign companies being successful bidders are companies legally responsible to execute the ventures entered into contracts with PGCB for design, manufacture and supply, installation, testing and commissioning etc of the projects. As the activities of the company had been done in exchange of foreign currency, consequently, its activities may be treated as "export/deemed export" if fulfills the pre-condition of being registered entities under the VAT Act in Bangladesh not the writ petitioner company as it is a sub-contractor only. Sub-contractors are not eligible to get drawbacks under rule 31A of the VAT Rules, 1991.
14. Besides, section 13(3) of the VAT Act, 1991 states that-
(৩) “মহাপরিচালক, শুল্ক রেয়াত ও প্রত্যর্পণ পরিদপ্তর”, সরকারী গেজেটে জারীকৃত আদেশ দ্বারা, কোন রপ্তানিকারককে প্রকৃত রপ্তানির বিপরীতে চালানভিত্তিক বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, রপ্তানি পণ্যের উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সম্পর্ক (input-output co-efficient) এর ভিত্তিতে নির্ধারিত সমহার (flat rate) এ রপ্তানিকৃত পণ্যে ব্যবহৃত উপকরণের উপর পরিশোধিত পরিমাণ উপ-ধারা (১) এ উল্লিখিত শুল্ক ও করসমূহ প্রত্যর্পণের নির্দেশ প্রদান করিতে পরিবেন।”
15. Thus it is clear that the concerned Department of NBR has power to conclude input-output co-efficient pursuant to and to grant drawback to the exporter on the duties and taxes paid on inputs used in the manufacturing of exported/deemed exported goods on that basis. For this reason, the impugned orders issued by the writ respondent no. 5 regretting to approve input-output co-efficient prior to granting drawback is lawful.

24. However, in the present case no such right was vested upon the respondent company as it was in no way entitled for drawbacks/tax rebates as vowed in the parent law. Hence, any plea of against retrospection is not sustainable in the eye of law. Misinterpretation of the laws at their sweet will cannot be a ground for statutory relieves and if any such drawbacks was paid that must be refunded.
25. In the present case, the related enactment concerning “drawback” of VAT tax of the parent law i.e. VAT Act, 1991 is section 13 and rule 31A is the subordinate legislation thereof, which is fairly consistent with the parent act. The impugned explanation is another type of delegated legislation irrespective of its status in the eye of law. At the same time the Office Order, dated 04.08.2013 i.e. Annexure- E(4)of the writ petition is too another subordinate legislation as per Rule 38 of VAT Rules, 1991.

সংস্থা কর্তৃক প্রাথমিকভাবে আহ্বানকৃত আন্তর্জাতিক দরপত্রের আওতায় কার্যাদেশ প্রাপ্ত মূল দেশিয় নিবন্ধিত প্রতিষ্ঠানকে রপ্তানি সুবিধা প্রদান করা হয়। পরবতীতে কার্ধাদেশ প্রাপ্ত মূল দেশিয় নিবন্ধিত প্রতিষ্ঠানকে রপ্তানি সুবিধা প্রদান করা হয়। পরবর্তীতে উক্ত মূল কার্যাদেশ প্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠান কক যদি একই প্রকল্পে পণ্য / সেবা সরবরাহের লক্ষ্যে পুনরায় পত্রিকায় দরপত্র বিজ্ঞপ্তি আহবান করে কোন দ্বিতীয় পক্ষকে সাব-কন্ট্রাক্টর নিয়ণগ করা হয় অথবা পণ্য/সেবা সরবরাহের কার্যাদেশ প্রদান করা হয় সেক্ষেত্রে যেহেতু নতুন করা বাংলাদেশ সরকার কোন বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা প্রাপ্ত হয় না, সেহেতু পণা/সেবা সরবররাহ দ্বিতীয়বার রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য হওয়ার কোন আইনগত সুষণগ নেই। প্রকল্প সম্পাদনের জন্য যে স্বক্কার সাথে প্রাথমিক চুক্তি সম্পাদিত হয় শুধুমাত্র এ স্ব্কার জন্য পণ্য বা সেবার সরবরাহ বা কার্যসম্পাদন রপ্তানি বলে গণ্য। অন্যকোন সরবরাহকারী এক্ষেত্রে বিবেচনার সুয়োগ নেই। কারণ এক্ষেত্রে প্রকল্প/চুক্তি সম্পাদনে মূল কার্যাদেশপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের কার্যক্রম রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য হওয়ায় সরবরাহ চেইনে পরিশোধিত পূর্ববর্তী শুল্ক-কর প্রত্যর্পণ প্রদান করার বিধান করা হয়েছে। তাই, প্রকল্প সম্পাদনে প্রাথমিকভাবে চুক্তিবদ্ধ স্বা রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য” কার্যক্রম করে বিধায় এ সুবিধা প্রাপ্ত হবে, অন্যকেউ নয়।
৫। এছাড়া, পাবলিক প্রকিউরমেন্ট আইন, ২০০৬ এর ধারা ৩ এর দফা (ঘ) অনুযায়ী কোন উন্নয়ন, বিদেশী রাষ্ট্র বা সংস্থার সহিত সরকারের সম্পাদিনত কোন খণ, অনুদান বা অন্যকোন চুক্তির অধীন কোন পণ্য, কার্য বা সেবা ক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে পাবলিক প্রকিউরমেন্ট আইন, ২০০৬ এবং পাবলিক প্রকিউরমেন্ট রুল, ২০০৮ এর বিধান পরিপালন বাধ্যতামূলক । অর্থাৎ মূলা সংযোজন কর বিধিমালা, ১৯৯১ এর বিধি ৩১ক এর আওতায় পণ্য বা সেবা সরবরাহ কার্যক্রম“রপ্তানিকৃত বলিয়া গণ্য” হতে হলে যেকোন স্থানীয় বা আন্তর্জাতিক দরপত্র কার্যক্রম পাবলিক প্রকিউরমেন্ট রুল, ২০০৮ এর বিধান মোতাবেক সংঘটিত হওয়ার আইনি বাধ্যবাধকতা রয়েছে। কোন সংস্থা বা প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক পাবলিক প্রকিউরমেন্ট, রুল, ২০০৮ অনুসরণপূর্বক দরপত্র কার্ধক্রম সম্পন্ন না করলে সেক্ষেত্রে বিধি ৩১ক এ উল্লিখিত রপ্তানি সংশ্লিষ্ট সুবিধাদি প্রযোজ্য হবে না।
০৬। সম্প্রতি কিছু কিছু প্রতিষ্ঠান সুল্য সংযযাজন কর বিধিমালা, ১৯৯১ এর বিধি ৩১ক এর অপব্যবহার করে রাজস্ব ফাকি দিচ্ছে মর্মে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের গোচরীভূত হয়েছে। তাই এ জাতীয় প্রতিষ্ঠানের কার্যক্রম নিবিড় মনিটরিং করে প্রয়োজনে নিরীক্ষা কার্ধক্রম সম্পাদনের মাধ্যমে আইনানুগ রাজন্ব আদায় করার জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট সকলকে নির্দেশক্রমে অনুরোধ করা হলো। বর্ণিতাবস্থায়, উপরোক্ত নির্দেশনা মোতাবেক যথাযথ আইনানুগ পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণের জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট সকলকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো ।

অনেক ক্ষেত্রে দেখা যায়, দেশের সরকারী, আধাসরকারী, স্থায়ত্বশাসিত প্রতিষ্ঠানের আন্তর্জাতিক দরপত্রের বিপরীতে বিদেশী কোন প্রতিষ্ঠান কার্যাদেশ প্রাপ্ত হয় এবং উক্ত কার্ধাদেশের অধীন সরবরাহতব্য পণ্য সংগ্রহের লক্ষ্যে চুক্তিবদ্ধ বিদেশী প্রতিষ্ঠান বৈদেশিক ঋণপত্র এবং বৈদেশিক মুদ্রার বিনিময়ে দেশের অভ্যন্তরে পণা সরবরাহের জন্য বাংলাদেশের কোন শিল্প কারখানার সাথে চুক্তিবদ্ধ হয়ে থাকে । আন্তর্জাতিক দরপত্রের মাধ্যমে কার্যাদেশ প্রাপ্ত বিদেশী প্রতিষ্ঠান বাংলাদেশ ব্যতীত তৃতীয় কোন দেশ হতে খণপত্রের মাধ্যমে পণ্য সংগ্রহ করে বাংলাদেশে পণ্য সরবরাহ করতে পারে। তবে সেক্ষেত্রে বাংলাদেশে বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা প্রাপ্তি থেকে বঞ্চিত হবে । এ সকল বিবেচনায় কার্যাদেশ প্রাপ্ত বিদেশী প্রতিষ্ঠান বাংলাদেশী উৎপাদক প্রতষ্ঠানকে খণপত্র দিয়ে বৈদেশিক মুদ্রায় পণ্য সংগ্রহকরন পূর্বক বাংলাদেশে সরবরাহ করলে তা রপ্তানি হিসাবে গণ্য করা যৌক্তিক। এ ধরণের Transaction এর ক্ষেত্রে বৈদেশিক খণপত্র এবং বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা যথাযথ প্রক্রিয়া অনুসরণপূর্বক বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের মাধ্যমে প্রত্যাবসিত হচ্ছে। এ জাতীয় পণ্য সরবরাহকে রপ্তানি হিসেবে পণ্য করা হলে একদিকে বৈদেশিক মুদ্র অর্জন, কর্মসংস্থানের সুযোগ ও সম্পন্ন পণ্য সামগ্রীকে স্বীকৃতি প্রদান করার সুযোগ সুষ্টি হবে। ২০১৩ - ২০১৪ অর্থ বছরের বাজেটে অর্থ আইন, ২০১৩ এর মাধ্যমে মূল্য সংযণজন কর আইন, ১৯৯১ এর ধারা ২৫(শ)ই এ বৈদেশিক ষুদ্রার বিনিময়ে ওলী অভ্যন্তরে সরবরাহকুত রাহকৃত পণ্য বা সেবাও রপ্তানীকৃত বলে গণ্য হবে মর্মে নতুন বিধান সংযোজিত হয়েছে। বন্ড সুবিধাভদেশী কোন প্রতিষ্ঠান একই কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করলে উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য বিধান/নীতিমালা সুস্পষ্ট হওয়া প্রয়োজন।

<u>27. The High Court Division as well as the respondent heavily relied upon the abovementioned Annexure-E(4). Consequently the same must not be directly or indirectly in conflict with the provisions of the enabling law. On perusal of the concerned parent act, rules and the aforementioned delegated legislations our considered view is that the Annexure-E(4)is inconsistent with provisions spelled out in the parent Act and Rules. At the same time the impugned explanation is the true and exact expression of what enacted in the parent Act and Rules. In addition, it is a revenue generating issue of the state. Public and higher State interest cannot be defeated for the sake of misleading subordinate legislation and procedural glitches. If these are the situations, as the highest court of the land, we opine that the Appellate Division should invoke its mandate under article 104 of the Constitution of Bangladesh for doing complete justice for the national interest. In the case of A.F.M. Naziruddin vs. Mrs. Hameeda Banu reported in 1992 12 BLD (AD) 261 Appellate Division observed that-</u>
<u>“Considering the vagaries of legal proceedings and the technicalities involved in adjudication, Art 104 of the Constitution has invested, as a measure of abundant caution, the last Court of the country with wide power, so it may forestall a failure of justice and do complete justice in an appropriate case. It is an extraordinary procedure for doing justice for completion of or putting an end to a cause or matter pending before this Court.”</u>
28. In this view of the matter, we are, therefore, of the considered view that if we don’t allow the appeal considering the vagaries of legal proceedings and the technicalities involved in adjudication as mentioned above it will be a total fiasco of justice.
29. Accordingly, we find merit in the submissions of the learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioners and the submissions of the Counsel of the respondent exposed having less than merit worthy, however, we opine that it is worth disposing of the petition, rather, than allow leave for saving time.
30. The reason elaborated above we find that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division do call for interference. In the result, the Civil Petition for Leave Appeal is disposed of. Impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside without any order as to cost.
End.

full_judgment:
MD. NURUZZAMAN, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 20.03.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.7901 of 2002 making the Rule absolute.
2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein as the writ petitioners filed the Writ Petition No.7901 of 2002 before the High Court Division stating, inter-alia, that Bangladesh Publisher and Book Seller Association is an association of the book publishers and sellers and persons engaged in the business of books. It has its own Articles and Memorandum of Association and also has elected Executive Committee consisting of 27 members.
3. The said Association was formed for conducting various affairs relating to publication and sale of book and for that purpose several Standing Committee, Sub-Committee have been formed.
4. Like other Standing Committee, there is a Committee namely, Creative Literature Standing Committee constituted by the Association from amongst its members and the writ respondent Nos.4-15 were Secretaries of various Standing committee and representatives of the Association.
5. Recently the writ petitioner Nos.1 and 2 came to learn that recommendation was made to the Government for granting Licence to a Samity under the name and style Bangladesh Gayan-OSrijonshil Prokashak Samity. The writ petitioners raised objection to the Deputy Secretary and the Director, Trade.
6. Organizations, Ministry of Commerce and requested not to grant such licence. On earlier occasion, similar attempt was also made but the same was dropped.
7. In spite of the said objection, licence No.34 of 2002 dated 17.11.2002 was granted in favour of added respondent No.17-petitioner.
8. The lience was granted in contravention of the Trade Organizations Ordinance, 1961.
9. The purposes and objects of the writ petitioner as respondent No.1 Association and those of the added respondent No.17 are similar.
10. The High Court Division by order dated 14.12.2002 issued Rule and stayed operation of the said impugned licence granted in favour of the added respondent No.17-petitioner, namely, Bangladesh Gayan-O-Srijonshil Prokashak Samity.
11. The respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein as writ petitioners filed the said writ petition without impleading the added respondent No.17- petitioner herein, Bangladesh Gayan-OSrijonshil Prokashak Samity in the said writ petition although they have challenged the licence granted in favour of the added respondent No.17-petitioner and obtained an order of stay in its absence.
12. The added respondent No.17-petitioner filed an application for being added as the respondent No.17 in the writ petition and the High Court Division allowed the said application and added the petitioner as respondent No.17 in the said writ petition.
13. The added respondent No.17-petitioner contested the said writ petition by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating, amongst others that, after meeting all the legal requirements, 26 (twenty six) members of this added respondent No.17-petitioner’s Association obtained Trade Organizations Licence No.34 of 2002, dated 17.11.2002 from the office of the Director, Trade Organizations, Ministry of Commerce and formed a Trade Organization under the name and style বাংলাদেশ জ্ঞান ও সৃজনশীল প্রকাশক সমিতি (Bangladesh Gayan-O-Srijonshil Prokashak Samity). Thereafter, the added respondent No.17- petitioner’s Association was registered under section 28 of the Companies Act, 1994 bearing Registration No.C-531(44)/2002, dated 27th November, 2002. <u>34. On perusal of the notices (Annexure 8 and 8/1) we find that these were not published in two national daily newspapers as mandatorily required. The concerned daily newspapers named as “Dainik Sabuj Bangla” and “Dainik Sonali Barta” are in no way national dailies, not only that from the contents of the notice published in those papers it appears that the notice was not published /circulated with a view to formation of a new organization as required by the law, rather, its contents exposed that there is already a organization and meeting of that committee would be held for transaction of the business of that committee. We are, therefore, of the view that notice was not in accordance with the provision of law as contemplate therein.</u>
35. As the notices were not published in the national dailies as required by law, it was not possible for the writ petitioners-respondents to file objections duly. Here, it is evident that presence of an underground campaign to deceive the writ petitioners-respondents from resorting prescribed relieves. In this connection, presence of fraudulent collusion from the part of government officials with the present appellants could also be inferred. It is a settled principle that fraud vitiates everything. In this point reliance could be placed upon the ratio propounded in the cases Government of Bangladesh and Ors. Vs Sadeque Ahmed Nipu and Ors. and Qumrun Nessa Vs. Mrs. Mahfuza Begum and others reported in 26 BLC (AD) (2021) 214 and 2016 36 BLD (AD) 1 respectively.
36. In the case of Mohammad Idrish Vs East Pakistan Timber Merchants Group, Registrar of Joint Stock Companies, East Pakistan reported in 20 DLR SC (1968)355 it was held that-
“For the same reason we are also of the view that section 12 of the Trade Organizations Ordinance, 1961, cannot take away the jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 98 so far as the correction of the acts of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies is concerned. It only provides a separate method for the resolving of the internal disputes of such organizations.”
<u>37.  In the case of Kartic Das Gupta Vs Election Commission of Bangladesh and others reported in 8 ADC (AD) 578, it has been held that before going into the merit of a Writ Petition, the first and primary duty of the court is to see whether the Writ Petition itself is maintainable in law or whether the writ-petitioner has got any interest in the subject matter which, if not protected, shall cause him to suffer injury.</u>
<u>38. With these 'ratio's in view, we find that High Court Division vividly discussed the maintainability issue of the writ petition itself. And it was held that the writ petition is maintainable as because the provision of appeal under section 15 of the Ordinance is not applicable and the appeal is not an equally efficacious/alternative remedy for the petitioner as government itself issued the impugned licence under Section 3 (2)(d) read with rule 3(8). Accordingly we approve the High Court Division’s rhetoric in this regard that an appeal against the issuance of the impugned licence tantamount to an appeal against the Caesar to the Caesar. As the writ petitioners are very much aggrieved by the decision passed by the government concurring with findings of the High Court Division as far as it concerns the maintainability we too opine that the writ petitioners are entitled to invoke their constitutional right under Article 102 of the constitution.</u>

“No licence shall be granted to a trade organisation unless the promoters or organisers thereof have, before its formation, by a notice published ina) at least two national daily newspapers, in the case of a trade organisation intended to be formed on all-Bangladesh basis; (b) a local or regional newspaper, in the case of any other trade organisation, declared their intention to form the trade organisation and the aims and objects thereof.”

Except some written statements that the said daily newspapers named as “Dainik Sabuj Bangla” and “Dainik Sonali Barta” where required prior notices were published as per section 3(7) of the Trade Organizations Ordinance, 1961; there submitted no grain of evidence/documents to prove that the dailies were National Daily Newspapers.
<u>41. Section 3(8) of the Trade Organizations Ordinance, 1961 is as such: “No trade organisation shall function or engage in any activities without first obtaining a licence under this Ordinance”</u>

43. In addition, it was contended that in 1997 one of such attempts for procuring the impugned licence was made and Government asked for the opinion of the writ petitioner on 14.07.1997 through Memo. No. FBCCI/43-BAM/912 whereupon the writ petitioner association requested not to issue such licence and the matter was dropped there. This means that a formal objection was pending before the licensing authority at the time of issuing the impugned license. As per rule 3(7) of the Trade Organizations Rules 1994 any objection pending concerning license should be considered. The Rule is as such:
“(৭) লাইসেন্স প্রদানের বিষয় বিবেচনার জন্য ডাইরেক্টর উদ্যোক্তাগণের নিকট হইতে সংশ্লিষ্ট যে কোন তথ্য বা কাগজপত্র তলব করিতে পারিবেন এবং উপ-বিধি (২) মোতাবেক কোনো আপত্তি বা পরামর্শ প্রেরিত হইয়া থাকিলে তাহা বিবেচনা করিবেন।”
44. However, it is not evident that that objection lodged by the present appellants-writ petitioners on 14.07.1997 through Memo. No. FBCCI/43-BAM/912 was in any way considered prior to the issuance of the impugned license.
<u>45. As the concerned notices were not published in any national daily newspapers recognized by persons of ordinary prudence and the aforesaid objection was not considered, these vitiated the whole process of licensing. Because, here licensing authority did not comply with the procedure established by law, did not act in accordance with the provisions of law, acted malafide and violated principles of natural justice. If it’s so, then established principle of law is that even if there is a ouster/non-obstante clause in any law, yet court has ample jurisdiction to review judicially whether the authority followed established principle of law or not.</u>
46. In the case of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and Others vs. Md. Idrisur Rahman, Advocate and Others reported in 17 BLT(AD) 231 stating that-
“…… the principle of natural justice is to be observed in a proceeding affecting a person or property or other rights of parties concerned. Accordingly, the Court, thus, always adds rider to the observance of the principle of natural justice in the exercise of power under the Constitution and other concerned laws of the land ...”
<u>47. In case of Rear Admiral AA Mustafa vs. Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary of Ministry of Defense, Dhaka cited in 51 DLR(AD) (1999) 146 this Division maintains that:</u>
<u>“As mala fide vitiates every exercise of power, a mala fide exercise of pleasure by the President under Article 134 of the Constitution can be brought within the purview of judicial review, if the other provisions of the Constitution are not a bar.”</u>
<u>48. In the case of M.M. Ibrahim vs. Mizanul Haque Chowdhury and Ors. reported in 69 DLR(AD) (2017 ) 192 Appellate Division observed that:</u>
<u>“From the statements made in the leave petition, it is clear that the impugned order was passed behind the back of the leave petitioner as it does not appear that the copy of the application for modification was served upon him and/or he was given any chance of hearing before passing the impugned order. Therefore, we find substance in the submission of Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam that the impugned order was passed in complete violation of the principles of natural justice, i.e. without giving any chance of hearing to the petitioner and, as such, the impugned order cannot be sustained.”</u>
49. Accordingly, we find no merit in submissions of the learned Counsel of the appellant.
50. The reason elaborated above we find that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division does not call for any interference.
51. In the result, this Civil Appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost.
End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 07.07.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1827 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J.: This civil appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 07.07.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1827 of 1997 making the Rule absolute. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that the present respondents as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.65 of 1991 in the 1st Court of Senior Assistant judge, Rajshahi, impleading the present petitioners as defendants for partition of the suit land contending interalia that the suit land measuring .57 acres of land under S.A. Khatian No.178 belonged to Kasimuddin and Samir Mondal in equal share obtained through pattan; Their names were accordingly finally published in S.A. Khatian; The Plaintiff no.1 is the daughter of Kasimuddinis first wife; After the expiry or plaintiff no. l's mother said Kasimuddin again married defendant. Meher Nigar and out of that wedlock plaintiff no.2 was born; While possessing half of the suit land, said Kasimuddin died leaving daughters, widow Meher. Nigar and nephew Abdul Kader as his legal heirs; On the other hand, 3,l mir Mondal while possessing the rest half of the suit land died leaving defendant nos.2 and 3 as his heirs; After the death of Kasimuddin said Meher Nigar received her share from other lands and sold the same to Chandicharan Sarker and ethers; Said Abdul Kader sold his share received from Kasimuddin to Professor Mozaharul, Islam and others; The plaintiffs while enjoying half of the suit land with defendant nos.1-3 in ejmali gave authority to defendant no.1 for recording R.S. Khatian; After getting final record of the R.S. Khatian the plain-tiffs for the first time came to know that it was wrongly recorded in the name of defendants alone and hence constrained to file the suit for partition since there is no earlier partition by metes and bounds. 

3. Defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia that the suit land originally belonged to Damon Mondal who expired leaving behind son Samir Mondal and daughter Arjan Bibi as his heirs; Said Arjan Bibi gave up her share in favour of her brother; Said Samir Mondal died leaving minor son and daughter defendant nos.1 and 2 and widow defendant no.3 as his heirs; Since then defendants are owning and possessing the suit land; R.S. Khatian was correctly recorded in their names; Since S.A. Khatian was wrongly recorded half of the land in the name of Kaimuddin the plaintiffs taking that opportunity filed this false suit which is liable to be dismissed. 

4. Plaintiffs in support of their case examined 4(four) witnesses and produced 4(four) rent receipts which are arked as exhibit-1 series, certified copy of S.A. Khatian no.178 marked as exhibit-2 and certified copy of C.S. Khatian no. 244 marked as exhibit-2.(Kha). On the other hand the defendants examined 5(five) witnesses and produced R.S. Khatian no.328 which is marked as exhibit-'Ka', S.A. Khatian no.178 and 2(two) rent' receipts marked as exhibit-'Kha', 'Kha(1)' and 'Kha(2)', death certificate of Kasimuddin marked as exhibit-'Ga' and certified copy of register relating to death of Kasimuddin marked as exhibit-'Gha' and 'Gha(1)', 2(two) photocopy of the letters sent by the Rajshahi Univerity to Samir Mondal which are marked as exhibit-'Uma' and `Uma(1)', certified copy of the sale deed sold by Meher Nigar which is marked as exhibit-'Cha'. 

5. After hearing the parties and perusing the record, learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 22.01.1994. Being dissatisfied, the defendants as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.71 of 1994 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rajshahi, which was heard on transfer by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Rajshahi. 

6. Upon hearing the parties and perusing the record, learned Additional District Judge allowed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 04.03.1997 reversing findings of the trial court. 

7. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiffs-respondents as petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.1827 of 1997 before the High Court Division under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Upon hearing the petitioners, a Single Bench of the High Court. Division issued rule. The defendants as opposite parties contested the rule. 

8. After hearing both the parties, a Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute vide judgment and order dated 07.07.2008. 

9. Feeling aggrieved, the defendants-opposite parties as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2341 of 2008 and obtained leave granting order dated 05.10.2009. Consequently, present civil appeal arose. 

10. Mr. A. M. Aminuddin, learned Advocate for the petitioners after taking us through the leave granting order and judgment and order passed by the High Court. Division as well as courts below submits that the High Court Division erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order having failed to appreciate that the plaintiffs have not been able to prove the 'pat tan' by which the plaintiffs-respondents claiming their right, title and interest in the suit land. He also submits that the appellate court below as a final court of facts controverted findings of the trial court after discussing evidences and materials on record and thus came to a proper decision as such the High Court Division has erred by interfering with the findings of fact by the appellate court below. He next submits that the High Court Division has not been able to find any misreading and non-reading of evidences and misconstruction of documents by the appellate court below and as such the impugned judgment and order is not tenable in law and liable to be set aside. He further submits that it is cardinal principal of law that the plaintiffs must prove their own case and they cannot win on the lacuna of the defendants but the High Court Division as well as the trial court found that the defendants have not been able to prove their case and as such the plaintiffs have title and possession in the suit land which resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

11. On the other hand, Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas learned Advocate appearing for the respondent nos.1-6 in support of the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division submits that the suit for partition simpliciter without prayer for title and khan possession in the suit land is not maintainable. The learned Advocate though admits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their 'pattan' by which they are claiming their title in the suit land but submits that the defendants also failed to prove their case by adducing documents inasmuch as the burden of proof also lies upon the defendants under section 103 of the Evidence Act and there is no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. 

12. Heard learned Advocate for the parties. Perused the papers/documents contained in the paper book. 

13. Admittedly, the plaintiffs' case is that the suit land belonged to their predecessor. Kasimuddin and defendants predecessor Samir Mondal in equal share Obtained through 'pattan'. The very basis of plaintiffs claim is the 'pattan'. But the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement of their predecessor' Kasimuddin. The P. W.1 Abdul Gafur, husband of the plaintiff no.1, deposed that: 
“ইসরাইল মন্ডল না: জমা জমি ভোগ দখল করিতে থাকাকালে সামির উদ্দীন, কসিম উদ্দীনকে কোর্ফা স্বতে পত্তন প্রদান করে । কসিম/সামির ১১ অংশেই দখল করিত।”

14. He stated in his cross examination: 
“কসিম সামির এর বন্দোবস্ত নেওয়া আমি দেখি নাই। সামির ও কসিমের বন্দোবস্ত নেওয়ার কাগজ কোর্টে দাখিল করিয়াছি। সত্য নহে যে, ঐ রকম কাগজ দাখিল করি নাই। আর, এস রেকর্ড যুদ্ধের আগেই তৈরি হয়। আর, এস রেকর্ভামলে আমরা কোন আপত্তি দেই নাই। রেকর্ড ঠিক মতই হইল বলে।”

15. Above statement of cross examination by the P.W.I nullify the averments made in paragraph. no.2 of the plaint that the plaintiffs while enjoying half of the suit land with defendant nos.1-3 in ejmali gave authority to defendant no.1 for recording R.S. Khatian and after getting final record of the R.S. Khatian the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that it was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants alone and thus constrained to file the suit. 

16. It may he mentioned here that the PW.1 produced 4(four) rent receipts which are marked as exhibit-I series, certified copy of S.A. Khatian No.178, marked as exhibit-2 and certified copy of C.S. Khatian No.244 marked as exhibit 2 f(Kha)'. But the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement in the name of their predecessor Kasimuddin by which they are claiming title in the suit land. 

17. On the other hand, the D.W.1 Md. Mofiz Uddin, defendant no.1, denying claim of the plaintiffs deposed that: 
“না: জমা জমি আমার দাদা ডুমন মন্ডলের ছিল। দাদা ডুমন মন্ডল না: জমা জমি ভোগ দখল করিতে
থাকাবস্থায় ১ পুত্র সমির ১ কন্যা আরজানকে রাখিয়া মারা যায়। ফুফু বড় লোকের ঘরে যাইয়া না: জমির দাবী ছাড়িয়া দেয়। আব্বাই না: জমি ১ দখল করিত। এস. এ আমলে আব্বার নামের সহিত কসিমুদ্দীনের নাম লিখিত হয়। না: জমিতে কসিমুদ্দীনের স্বত দখল ছিল না। এস, এ রেকর্ড ভুলক্রমে কসিমুদ্দীনের নাম হয় ।”

18. On perusal it appears that the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order without any independent findings and without adverting reasonings of the appellate court below arrived at a finding that: 
"The trial court properly sifted the statements of the P.Ws. the genealogy of ownership and inheritance in the suit land but the appellate court did not properly revert those observations and sift the statements of the witnesses of both the sides but abruptly came to a decision setting aside the judgments of the decrees of the trial court." 

19. And thereby made the rule absolute. The High Court Division failed to appreciate that the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement of their predecessor Kasimuddin by which they are claiming their title in the suit land and thereby erred in law to follow the cardinal principle of law that the plaintiffs must prove their own case and they cannot win on the lacuna of the defendants. 

20. It also appears that the High Court. Division failed to arrive any findings regarding misreading and misconstruction of evidence on record by the appellate court below. It is evident that the High Court Division did not at all discuss the evidence of possession adduced by the parties. Thus it is clear that without adverting to the reasonings given by the appellate court below which is the final court of facts, the High Court. 

21. Division erroneously passed the impugned judgment and order. 

22. In result, the appeal is allowed. The judgment and order dated 07.07.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1827 of 1997 is set aside and decree of the Additional District. Judge, Rajshahi, is restored. 

23. No order as to costs. 

End.
